mining_summaries: Mined 1117 tasks in .taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json (ids 11-1152) for fix-flavored language. ~946 matched loosely, but real recurring clusters concentrate in a handful of hotspot files: harness.py/task_knowledge_sync.py (project_root routing + stranded-task reconciliation, patched over a dozen times across months), TaskInterceptor/task_curator (dedup lock races and duplicate-task creation — ironically the tracker itself shows duplicate task IDs with identical titles, e.g. 999/1000, 1026/1028, 882/883, which is corroborating evidence of the exact dedup defect being chased), flag_dedup marker semantics in reconciliation (refixed 6+ times, still pending at 1146), graphiti_client/memory_service rebuild_entity_summaries (long chain of CancelledError-swallowing and structured-concurrency hardening), workflow.py's false-done/DONE-early-return guard (recurring premature-completion bug), merge_queue's plan-target false-positive drop guard, cargo_cli_error classifier tuning in verify.py, steward timeout/retry-cap hardening, dashboard burndown/costs test-quality churn, and usage_gate probe/leak races. Several themes have live pending/blocked tasks at the end of the id range (1135-1152), indicating the survey caught genuinely open frontiers, not just closed history. The single most striking recurrence is silent-failure/CancelledError-swallowing across at least 4 different modules (graphiti_client, memory_service, task backend, MemoryService.close) — a systemic pattern of async error paths being under-tested until an incident surfaces them.

Mining ~5,055 fix/amend/regression/red-main commits since 2026-01-01 (of ~45.9k total) across the seven subsystems shows a small number of bug classes account for most of the churn. The single biggest cross-cutting pattern is a two-phase workflow: a feature lands GREEN, then an immediate follow-up 'fix: resolve lint and type errors' or 'amend: apply reviewer suggestions' commit — this appears after nearly every feature commit in every subsystem and reflects the TDD-agent pipeline's own process (agent writes code, pre-commit/pyright catches drift, a forced second commit fixes it) rather than a code defect per se. Beneath that noise floor, real recurring bug classes cluster around: asyncio cancellation-safety gaps (CancelledError swallowed/mishandled) hit independently in merge-queue, workflow/harness, verify, fm-recon, and fm-memory; subprocess lifecycle hardening (start_new_session/terminate_process_group/killpg) applied piecemeal to 6+ separate call sites over many months; branch/task identity and metadata-shape drift (branch naming, metadata dict-vs-string, directory-vs-file paths) recurring in merge-queue, scheduler, and fm-task-layer; escalation/task dedup and phantom-completion (ghost-loop, zombie escalations, TOCTOU races) recurring in merge-queue, workflow, and escalation; and reconciliation's dedup-detector vs prompt-wording whack-a-mole in fm-recon. Warm-lane/worktree pool lifecycle races (bootstrap, orphan reuse, TOCTOU) are a persistent hotspot in git-worktrees. Usage-gate cap-message detection is a long-running whack-a-mole in shared-infra as the CLI's own cap-hit wording keeps changing.

clusters.architecture_notes: The subsystem is one god-class, SpeculativeMergeWorker (merge_queue.py:3701, ~5,700 lines of the 9,407-line file), running two coroutines: a merger loop (:6937) that creates merge commits (speculatively against the predecessor's merge SHA) and a verifier loop (:7494) that dispatch-fills verify hosts and finalizes heads in submission order, CAS-advancing main. Its __init__ (:3773-4152) declares ~60 instance fields: two plain semaphores (_speculation_slot, _merge_ahead_cap), six per-task counter dicts, five queues/deques an item migrates through (_queue → _lane_buffers → _verifier_queue/_redispatch → _inflight), and four "transient-window" side-fields (_inflight_req, _remerging_item, _finalizing_head, _dispatching_item) that exist solely so an item awaiting inside a call is not invisible to observability and permit audits. The recent 17-task refactor (df 1985-2002) extracted satellite modules, but they are function-bags that take the worker and mutate its privates (merge_drift.py:267-288, merge_shadow.py:1023-1072), or (merge_gates.py) deliberately import their own siblings back through merge_queue's re-export shim so old string-path monkeypatches keep working — the dependency graph is circular and the real namespace is still merge_queue (64 test files import from it). Item lifecycle state is encoded four redundant ways: container membership, a free-form phase:str on InflightEntry, an InflightStatus sentinel enum, and worker side-fields, with a vestigial _verify_phase dual-written alongside entry.phase (:8701-8702). Invariants are checked by after-the-fact census detectors (speculation_accounting_violations :5019, two_layer_invariants :4786, worktree_ledger_violations :5090) rather than enforced at transition time, and permit correctness depends on callers passing release_resources/chain_failed flags correctly (:7686-7939, :7872 `release_resources=not _entry_released`). A retired serial MergeWorker survives verbatim as a 384-line test fixture (orchestrator/tests/_serial_merge_worker.py) that production docstrings still cite as the byte-identical behavioral reference. Enormous docstrings carry the real contracts — nearly every invariant is prose-enforced.
clusters.cross_system_notes: Strong evidence in both directions with the scheduler/workflow and the fused-memory task store. The root gap: a merge landing (git main advance, owned by merge_queue) and the task's status=done write (fused-memory MCP, written by workflow via a callback) are not atomic and have no shared durable record, so a crash between them re-dispatches an already-merged task. Compensations are scattered across THREE subsystems: workflow.py carries pre-PLAN and post-PLAN ghost-loop guards with deliberately different semantics and a comment warning to keep both in sync (workflow.py:1642-1656); merge_queue re-detects already-merged branches inside classify_and_merge (merge_queue.py:2438-2472); scheduler.py grew a whole exception family (SetTaskStatusRejected/TerminalExitRejection/DoneGateRejection/ProvenanceValidationRejection, scheduler.py:90-160) for fused-memory's server-side phantom-done, terminal-exit and done_provenance gates — each a detector for the same missing atomicity guarantee. Fix history confirms recurrence: 7dfe0e69bc 'prevent ghost-loop when merged task never reaches DONE', e6d958a133 'close pre-PLAN ghost-loop recovery race that DONEd phantom reify tasks', 492bb8f126 'stop zombie escalation storm on out-of-band task completion', dc33b760c8 'break stash_failed requeue ghost loop with defense-in-depth'.

findings.title: Speculation-permit conservation is audited by a five-location census instead of owned permit tokens
findings.problem: A permit is just an anonymous decrement of asyncio.Semaphore _speculation_slot; nothing records WHICH item holds one. So the conservation check _inflight_speculative_count (merge_queue.py:4923-5005) must enumerate every place a permit-holding item can physically be: _inflight entries, _verifier_queue._queue internals, _redispatch (added by task 2063), _finalizing_head (added by task 2096 after the detector false-alarmed for entire 20-60min head verifies), and _dispatching_item (task 2096 again, for the dispatch-gap await). Every new await point in the pipeline silently creates a new uncounted window and a new false-positive class. Releases are scattered across ~10 raw self._speculation_slot.release() sites (:6321, :6425, :7824, :8279, :8932) plus SpeculationController's merger-side half plus _resolve_and_release's slot_held branch; callers must pass release_resources=False on POST-finalize paths (:7686, :7722, :7939) and even release_resources=not _entry_released (:7872) to avoid double-release — ownership phase is tracked in the caller's head. SpeculationController (task 1993) reified only the merger-side lifecycle; its docstring explicitly says verifier-side releases keep hitting the raw semaphore, and the semaphore must stay unbounded specifically to tolerate a known double-release race.
findings.proposal: Introduce a SpecPermit token object and a PermitLedger as the single owner of the semaphore. acquire() returns a SpecPermit registered in a live set; the token is stored ON the item (SpeculativeItem.permit / InflightEntry.permit) and travels with it through every queue, park, dispatch and finalize; release(token) is idempotent (token.released flag) and asserts the token is live, killing both the double-release race and the release_resources caller flags. Conservation becomes structural: slot_available + len(ledger.live) == depth by construction, regardless of where items sit — the five-location census, _dispatching_item, and the _finalizing_head census term all die. Ban raw _speculation_slot access with a grep-guard test (the repo already uses this idiom for SpeculativeItem construction sites). Same treatment for _merge_ahead_cap (counts_against_cap field becomes a CapPermit).

findings.title: Item lifecycle is encoded by container membership plus four side-fields and three parallel status mechanisms — no state machine
findings.problem: Where an item IS in its lifecycle is derivable only by knowing which of five containers holds it (_queue, _lane_buffers, _verifier_queue, _redispatch, _inflight) plus whether one of four worker transient fields points at it (_inflight_req :3898, _remerging_item :3908, _finalizing_head :3913-3919, _dispatching_item :3921-3931 — each added by a separate bug fix for an 'invisible window'). On top of that, InflightEntry carries a free-form phase: str ('verifying'/'gate_reverify'/'finalizing', merge_types.py:954, written at merge_queue.py:8702/8801/8864), a separate InflightStatus sentinel enum (DROPPED/REQUEUED/... merge_types.py:890), AND vestigial _verify_phase/_verify_item fields dual-written 'to avoid a large diff' (:3900-3906, :8701, :8800, :8863) that previously caused a stale phantom snapshot entry (comment at :5552). Every consumer that needs global state — snapshot() (:5468, sections 0/1/1b/2/3 mirror the census), speculation_accounting_violations, the request-liveness ledger — re-derives it by scanning all locations, and the consumers have already diverged once (task 2068: _redispatch-parked items were counted by the audit but missing from snapshot; _dispatching_item is deliberately in the audit but NOT in snapshot).
findings.proposal: Add an ItemLifecycle registry keyed by request_id with an explicit state enum (QUEUED, LANE_BUFFERED, MERGING, AWAITING_VERIFY, REDISPATCH_PARKED, DISPATCHING, VERIFYING, GATE_REVERIFY, FINALIZING, TERMINAL) and a legal-transition table enforced by a single transition(rid, from, to) method that raises/escalates on illegal moves. Queues keep holding the objects, but every put/pop site calls transition() — the four transient side-fields become the states DISPATCHING/MERGING/FINALIZING instead of nullable fields to remember to clear in finally blocks. snapshot(), the permit audit and the liveness ledger become single reads of the registry, guaranteeing they can never disagree. Delete _verify_phase/_verify_item and the free-form phase string (phase = registry state).

findings.title: Merge-landed→task-done is non-atomic across subsystems; six ghost-loop/phantom-done detectors compensate in three places
findings.problem: The merge queue advances main (git, in-process) and the task's done status is written afterwards to fused-memory via a callback chain that can be lost on crash/restart. The missing guarantee — a durable, consultable record that branch X landed as SHA Y for task Z — is compensated by independent detectors: workflow.py:1642 pre-PLAN ghost-loop recovery plus a second post-PLAN guard with deliberately different semantics and a comment ordering maintainers to keep both in sync; merge_queue.py:2438 already-merged is_ancestor detection inside classify_and_merge (with its own uncommitted-work sub-guard); scheduler.py:90-160's exception family mirroring fused-memory's server-side phantom-done/terminal-exit/provenance gates; plus 'terminally mark unknown-branch merge requests' (4a98702a48). Each detector was added by a separate incident and each has had its own false-positive/race fixes (e6d958a133 fixed the pre-PLAN guard DONEing phantom reify tasks). MergeQueueStore (task 1772) already journals accepted requests durably but records nothing on the landing side.
findings.proposal: Extend MergeQueueStore with a landed-outbox table written in the same code path as the CAS advance (task_id, branch_tip_sha, advanced_sha, wall time) — git's reflog proves the advance, the row makes it queryable. Make it the single source of truth: (1) scheduler consults it before dispatch (replacing workflow's two is_ancestor guards with one lookup + one is_ancestor confirmation), (2) a startup reconciler drives status=done with merged-provenance from unconsumed rows (replacing the lost-callback window), (3) ghost-loop detection collapses to 'row exists but task not done'. The fused-memory server-side gates stay (defense in depth at the boundary) but the orchestrator-side guard count drops from ~6 to 1.

findings.title: The 17-task refactor extracted the wrong seam: satellites are function-bags over worker privates, wired through circular reach-back imports frozen by test monkeypatch paths
findings.problem: The df 1985-2002 split moved text, not state or dependency edges. merge_drift.py:267-288 and merge_shadow.py:1023-1072 take the live worker and read/write its privates (_drift_land_count, _runner_quarantine, _drift_check_tasks, _shadow_compare_tasks, _shadow_state_path) — the state stayed in the god-class, so the seam is fake. Worse, merge_gates.py functions import their own co-located siblings BACK through merge_queue at function level (:361 'reaches back through orchestrator.merge_queue._check_post_merge_equivalence ... so the existing suite's string-path monkeypatches stay effective', also :400, :439, :533, :1353, :1430), creating a deliberate circular dependency whose only purpose is preserving 7 test monkeypatch string paths; merge_queue.py carries 9 noqa:F401 re-export blocks (~70 names) and 64 test files still import from merge_queue. Consequence: merge_queue.py stays the #1 churn file because every satellite change still routes through it, patching one namespace while calls resolve through the other is a live silent-divergence hazard, and the god-class __init__ keeps absorbing each satellite's state fields with paragraph-long ownership comments (e.g. the SuffixConflictTracker lambda-injection block :4096-4130).
findings.proposal: Finish the extraction along state lines: give each satellite an owning object holding ITS state — DriftDetectorSchedule(_drift_land_count, _runner_quarantine, _drift_check_tasks), ShadowCompareScheduler(_shadow_state_path, _shadow_compare_tasks) — instantiated as one worker field each, mirroring what SuffixConflictTracker already did for suffix state. Kill the reach-back convention with a one-time mechanical test migration (repoint the 7 string-path monkeypatches to the defining module), then delete the function-level back-imports and shrink the re-export shim to the public surface (MergeRequest, MergeOutcome, enqueue_merge_request, SpeculativeMergeWorker). Enforce the direction with an import-linter contract: merge_gates/merge_drift/merge_shadow/merge_liveness must not import merge_queue.

findings.title: Branch identity is stringly-typed; shape-tolerance is patched in at every consumer instead of parsed once at the boundary
findings.problem: MergeRequest.branch is a bare str that historically arrives either bare ('4778') or prefixed ('task/4778'), so correctness depends on consumption-site normalizers added one incident at a time: canonical_queued_branch_name (git_ops.py:737-753, 'prepend unless already present'), GitOps.resolve_queued_branch_ref with try-both-forms plus an explicit tie-break rule (git_ops.py:3968-3997), MergeQueueStore.record() stripping the prefix at journal-write (merge_queue_store.py:110-117) while the recovery path re-canonicalizes shape-tolerantly (merge_queue_store.py:301-304), and ~8 inline f'{branch_prefix}{...}' constructions scattered through git_ops (:1246, :1307, :1770, :2649, :3378). Every new feature that touches branch names (recovery, journaling, warm lanes, suffix graph) has re-introduced the ambiguity and required another central-resolver retrofit; the resolver at 3 call sites was itself a 3-commit propagation task (1911).
findings.proposal: Parse, don't validate: a frozen QueuedBranch value type in merge_types.py with fields bare_id and full_name and a single classmethod parse(raw, branch_prefix) that is the ONLY place prefix logic lives. MergeRequest.branch becomes QueuedBranch (constructed at the two entry boundaries: enqueue_merge_request and journal recovery); git refs are always built from .full_name. canonical_queued_branch_name, the try-both logic in resolve_queued_branch_ref, and the journal strip/re-add pair all die; a mixed-shape value becomes unrepresentable past the boundary. pyright then enforces the invariant at every one of today's drift sites for free.

findings.title: A retired serial worker and compat shims are load-bearing test anchors that freeze production structure
findings.problem: The retired serial MergeWorker survives verbatim as a 384-line frozen fixture (orchestrator/tests/_serial_merge_worker.py) because ~89 test constructions were never migrated; production merge_queue.py cites 'the test-local MergeWorker reference' 10 times as the behavioral spec its counters and outcomes must mirror 'byte-identically' (e.g. classify_and_merge's docstring :2400-2410, the _cas_retries/_post_merge_verify_timeouts/auto_heal_registry comments :3833-3910). Similarly _verify_and_advance (:9229) is a 'thin compat shim ... retained so the ~18 tests calling it directly stay green', and _verify_item/_verify_phase are write-only vestigial fields 'retained to avoid a large diff'. The effect is bidirectional coupling with the test suite's accidental structure: refactors must preserve retired-implementation quirks and dead namespaces, which is exactly why the 17-task refactor ended as re-export shims and reach-back imports (finding above) rather than a real decomposition — and why merge_queue.py remains the churn hotspot.
findings.proposal: Declare the speculative worker the sole spec and pay down the anchors: (1) migrate the ~18 _verify_and_advance direct-call tests to drive the public run()/merge() surface or a small test harness around _dispatch_item+_finalize_inflight, then delete the shim; (2) delete the write-only _verify_item/_verify_phase fields and their 4 dual-write sites; (3) freeze _serial_merge_worker.py usage with a ratchet test (no NEW imports of it) and strip the 10 'mirrors the test-local reference' claims from production docstrings so future agents stop treating the retired worker as normative; (4) adopt a convention (enforceable via grep-guard) that tests monkeypatch the defining module, unlocking shim deletion.

clusters.hotspot: workflow — orchestrator/src/orchestrator/workflow.py (8,835 lines, 604 commits, 226 fix/amend-class) plus steward.py, agents/roles.py, review_checkpoint.py, dry_run_unblock.py, artifacts.py
clusters.architecture_notes: TaskWorkflow is a single 8.8k-line god-class whose run() method drives PLAN→EXECUTE→VERIFY→REVIEW→MERGE inline, with 53 distinct mutable instance attributes acting as inter-phase side channels (_last_block_*, _inherited_break_info, _infra_hold_info, _zero_output_hang_info, _pending_resume_*, _merge_sha, state). The 'state machine' of the module docstring is nominal: WorkflowState is set via _enter_phase (workflow.py:1463), which emits events but enforces no legal-transition table, and 19 call sites jump states freely; WorkflowOutcome is a second parallel vocabulary; the fused-memory task-status row (22 set_task_status sites, server-side terminal guard only per task_status.py docstring) is a third; and metadata stamps (done_provenance, counters) are a fourth. Terminal decisions reach the harness through stashed _last_block_reason/_phase/_detail attrs read at harness.py:5173-5175 rather than a return type. Agent lifecycle lives in _invoke (6876), which derives capabilities from three parallel sources: AgentRole declarations in roles.py, name-string gate tuples _MCP_CONFIG_ROLES/_PLAN_TOOLS_ROLES (105-114), and hardcoded role.name checks. The steward is a separate per-task process-lifetime object, but the workflow learns its outcome only by forensic re-reads of the escalation queue and status row (L0-empty, L1-open, dismissed-within-timestamp-window, status-changed) — there is no typed result channel. Blocking/escalation policy is concentrated in the 350-line _mark_blocked (7702), an accretion of named incident patches (Fix A broadened, Fix C, Fix #2) with 58 call sites. run() ends in a seven-clause exception ladder (1919-2116) that re-classifies failures other subsystems raised, plus a finally block that sniffs sys.exc_info() to detect hard-cancel, coordinated by comment contract with harness.py's B2 synthetic_cancel guard. Anti-thrash guards are 8 ad-hoc integer/string counters in task metadata with bespoke parsing and best-effort persistence. Satellite modules (steward, review_checkpoint, dry_run_unblock) each independently catch AllAccountsCappedException and re-derive block dispositions. The real seams for decomposition are: terminal-decision/status ownership, steward RPC, merge-provenance lookup, and the agent-invocation capability gate.
clusters.cross_system_notes: Four clear cases of cross-system patching. (1) fused-memory's TaskInterceptor owns terminal-status legality server-side (task_status.py docstring: 'the orchestrator no longer guards transitions client-side'), so workflow grew client-side bypass-discrimination machinery to interpret rejections: the SetTaskStatusRejected/TerminalExitRejection handlers at run():1957-2012, _mark_blocked:7760, and _handle_terminal_exit_on_block:7524 — the legality contract lives in another process and workflow reverse-engineers its verdicts. (2) fused-memory's tasks.json auto-commit to main makes branch-SHA comparisons racy, forcing _has_prior_implementation (7261-7269) to require BOTH SHA-divergence AND iteration-log evidence — a dual-signal heuristic compensating for a missing 'main only advances via merge queue' guarantee. (3) shared.cli_invoke's AllAccountsCappedException escapes into workflow (1919), steward.py:653, review_checkpoint.py:192, and dry_run_unblock.py:341 — four independent catch sites (mined whack-a-mole f66a04d61f/6e905017c3/a946399937) because shared infra offers no boundary-level disposition, only a raw exception. (4) git_ops warm-lane faults (WarmLanePoolHardDown/Exhausted/DiskPressure) are triaged inside workflow's exception ladder (2014-2068) while the scheduler's per-tick watchdog is acknowledged in-comment as the primary defense — the same host-scoped condition is classified in two subsystems with a comment admitting the requeue-cap accounting is wrong for two of the three subclasses. Additionally task_status.ACTIVE_TASK_STATUSES is a hand-mirrored copy of fused-memory's reconciliation set, guarded only by a cross-package equality test.

findings.title: 'Already merged?' is answered by three divergent heuristic guards instead of one durable merge-provenance record
findings.problem: Because advance_main and the status=done write are not atomic (a run can die between them), the next run must re-derive 'did my work land?' forensically. Three guards do this with deliberately different semantics: pre-PLAN _recover_if_already_merged (workflow.py:7291, SHA-primary), the pre-EXECUTE already_on_main check (1776-1816, iteration-log-only — 'SINGLE SIGNAL' comment), and the merge-phase ancestor check. Comments at 1649-1654 and 1771-1775 explicitly warn 'do not collapse them' and 'if you change the is_ancestor/has_work logic, check both guards'. The shared heuristic _has_prior_implementation (7202-7289) is 90 lines of trade-off analysis defending against .task/ contamination, rebased-HEAD==base_commit, architect scratch, and fused-memory auto-commit races — each clause a past false-done incident.
findings.proposal: Make merge provenance a durable, write-ahead record instead of a heuristic: the merge queue writes a per-task journal entry (task_id → merge_sha, branch_tip_sha, ts) in the same critical section that moves refs/heads/main (it already stamps metadata.done_provenance on some paths — make it mandatory and ordered BEFORE the ref update, fsynced, e.g. a MergeJournal in the event_store or a git note on the merge commit). All three guards collapse to one MergeProvenance.lookup(task_id) call; _has_prior_implementation survives only as a legacy fallback behind the journal miss path. Enforce with a test that no code path can return WorkflowOutcome.DONE without either journal provenance or an explicit human done_provenance.

findings.title: Steward outcome is inferred from escalation-queue side effects and timestamp windows instead of a typed result
findings.problem: The workflow↔steward contract is mediated entirely through shared mutable state: after _await_steward_completion, _mark_blocked runs five probes to guess what the steward did — status in TERMINAL (workflow.py:7924), status=='deferred' (7961), L0-queue-empty (7938), L1-open (7946), and dismissed-L0s whose resolved_at ISO string falls inside a steward_window_start window (7913, 7980-7998, 'Fix A broadened'). run()'s ESCALATED branch duplicates the status-honoring subset with a comment 'Mirrors the inline returns inside _mark_blocked (~L3125–3168) but bypasses it' (1849-1873). Crucially there is no INTERRUPTED signal: steward_max_attempts=1 (steward.py:12) plus a wall-clock kill looks identical to 'steward failed', which is exactly the healthy-WIP-misdiagnosed-as-failure class in operator memory.
findings.proposal: Give TaskSteward.handle_escalation a typed StewardOutcome sum type returned (or queued on an asyncio channel) to the owning workflow: RESOLVED(resolution_text) | REESCALATED_L1(esc_id) | TERMINAL_DECISION(new_status) | INTERRUPTED(timeout|attempt_cap, wip_commits_present) | BUDGET_EXHAUSTED. The workflow branches on it in exactly one function; the escalation queue remains persistence/notification but stops being the RPC channel; the timestamp-window dismissal heuristic dies. INTERRUPTED with wip_commits_present routes to a resume-plan path instead of L1, encoding the 'triage WIP health before restarting' lesson structurally.

findings.title: Task terminal state is quadruplicated with no enforced transition table; harness contract is three stashed instance attributes
findings.problem: The same lifecycle is represented four ways that can disagree: WorkflowState set by _enter_phase (workflow.py:1463 — emits events, enforces nothing, 19 call sites), WorkflowOutcome return values, the fused-memory status row (22 set_task_status sites, legality enforced only server-side per task_status.py:3-6), and metadata stamps. The only client-side transition guard is the hand-rolled 'already DONE, ignoring late blocked transition' check at _mark_blocked:7742. Terminal context flows to the harness via the _last_block_reason/_last_block_phase/_last_block_detail side channel (775-777, written at 2065-2067, 2800-2801, 7751-7753; read at harness.py:5173-5175) — any BLOCKED/REQUEUED path that forgets to stash gets misattributed retry-cap accounting.
findings.proposal: Introduce a WorkflowStateMachine value object owning `state` with a legal-transition table (dict[WorkflowState, frozenset[WorkflowState]]) that raises on illegal transitions and makes DONE/CANCELLED absorbing — the 7742 guard becomes a property of the machine, not one method's memory. Replace the _last_block_* side channel with a TerminalReport dataclass (outcome, reason, phase, detail, category) that _mark_blocked constructs and run() returns; harness consumes the report, deleting the attr-poking at harness.py:5173. Runtime-assert on run() exit that WorkflowState, WorkflowOutcome, and the last-written status row are mutually consistent (one table maps outcome→allowed statuses).

findings.title: run()'s seven-clause exception ladder re-implements failure classification owned by other subsystems
findings.problem: run() ends with catches for AllAccountsCappedException (workflow.py:1919), _SessionBudgetExhausted (1929), SetTaskStatusRejected (1957), WarmLaneRequeue with a 3-subclass isinstance triage (2014-2068), VerifyInfraError (2070), bare OSError re-classified via verify.py's underscore-private _is_infra_oserror (2090, imported at :87), and broad Exception (2114) — each added after an exception 'escaped' a deeper handler. The comment at 2094-2097 even documents duplicating the generic path because Python can't re-raise into a sibling clause. The same cap exception is separately caught in steward.py:653, review_checkpoint.py:192, and dry_run_unblock.py:341 with independently-written dispositions; the warm-lane clause admits in-comment (2026-2044) that its requeue-cap accounting is wrong for two of three subclasses and defers to a scheduler change.
findings.proposal: Create one classify_failure(exc) -> BlockDisposition(category, escalate_to_human, requeue_kind, counts_against_requeue_cap, reason_prefix) table in a shared module (natural home: next to task_status.py, or shared/ since steward/review/dry-run also need it). _mark_blocked accepts a BlockDisposition; run() keeps one except clause per outcome kind (requeue / block / cancel) that consults the table. New failure types become table rows with a completeness test (every exported exception type in git_ops/verify/cli_invoke/usage_gate has a row), ending the per-call-site whack-a-mole and fixing the requeue-cap misaccounting in one place.

findings.title: Anti-thrash guards are eight untyped counters in task metadata with best-effort read-modify-write over the MCP boundary
findings.problem: Loop/thrash protection is implemented as ad-hoc metadata keys — consecutive_no_plan_failures, total_no_plan_failures, last_no_plan_main_sha, consecutive_infra_resume_failures, last_infra_resume_iteration_count, consecutive_merge_thrash, last_merge_outcome_signature, plus merge_first_enqueued_at — each parsed defensively (int(metadata.get(...) or 0) inside try/except at workflow.py:3422-3435), persisted best-effort ('failed to persist infra-resume thrash counter: log and proceed', 3456-3464, so the counter silently loses increments and the guard under-fires), and merged via the hand-rolled last-writer-wins _merge_fresh_metadata (3233-3280) whose own docstring admits 'memory_hints may be clobbered'. The concurrency story is a comment: 'same per-task concurrency assumption as the existing writer; no new hazard' (3381-3383). Each new thrash mode historically added a new counter cluster and a new fix task.
findings.proposal: Define one schema-versioned RetryLedger dataclass under a single metadata key (retry_ledger) with typed fields per guard, one load(validate-or-reset-loudly) and one persist path; guards become pure functions RetryLedger -> GuardVerdict. Make persist failure escalate (the guard exists to stop money-burning loops — silently losing an increment defeats it), or move the ledger into the .task/ artifacts dir where the workflow is the single writer and persistence is a local fsync, keeping only the final blocked verdict in metadata. Signature normalization (_normalize_cause_hint / _compute_merge_outcome_signature, 367-424) moves in as ledger methods so signature-keying can't be recomputed differently at different call sites.

findings.title: Agent capability wiring split across roles.py declarations and workflow.py name-string gate tuples
findings.problem: AgentRole.allowed_tools (roles.py:241, 307, ...) declares which MCP tools a role may call, but whether the backing servers are actually wired is decided elsewhere by name-string membership: _MCP_CONFIG_ROLES/_PLAN_TOOLS_ROLES tuples (workflow.py:105-114, consulted at 6925/6938), a hardcoded sandbox check role.name in ('implementer','debugger') (6913), a reviewer-prefix special case (6903-6909), and the role_key = role.name.split('_')[0] config-lookup convention (6892). The invariant is stated only in a comment (96-98: a role listing a tool 'MUST also appear here... or the session is told to call tools that do not exist'). SIMPLE_TASK shipped violating it: its success contract was unsatisfiable without the plan-tools server, so the fast path silently always fell through to the architect and its cost saving never materialized (comment at 109-114).

Add a module-import-time assertion in roles.py that any role whose allowed_tools reference fused-memory/escalation/plan-tools names declares the corresponding family — a new role that forgets fails at import, not weeks later in a watched project with no static .mcp.json.

findings.title: Cancellation is three parallel mechanisms with per-call-site opt-in, coordinated by comment contracts across files
findings.problem: Hard cancel (asyncio task.cancel from the harness) is detected in run()'s finally by sniffing sys.exc_info() for CancelledError (workflow.py:2154-2160), and correctness depends on a two-file comment contract with harness.py's B2 synthetic_cancel guard ('both must fire', 2148-2153; harness.py:5212-5223). Soft cancel (_cancel_event) is honored only where a call site opted in: _await_cancellable wraps exactly two awaits (1069, 5503), plus scattered is_set() checks (2312, 8776) — any other long await (steward waits, agent invocations, verify subprocesses) ignores soft-cancel until it finishes. _handle_soft_cancel (8691) then re-derives intent from a racy status read with a documented watcher-race caveat (8709-8720). The mined history shows this defect class being fixed one await at a time.
findings.proposal: One cancellation seam: run the workflow body under a CancelScope-style supervisor that converts both harness hard-cancel and _cancel_event into a single typed WorkflowCancelled(kind=hard|soft) control signal caught at exactly one place in run(); register terminal cleanups (lane release, config-dir cleanup, steward stop) in an ordered on_terminal list executed by the supervisor with the cancel kind as input, replacing the exc_info sniffing and the B1/B2 dual-guard coordination. Every future long await is covered by construction because it runs inside the scope, eliminating the opt-in gap.

findings.title: _SchedulerLike shadow protocol plus N hand-maintained fakes drift with every new scheduler dependency
findings.problem: workflow.py:212-253 defines a hand-copied structural protocol of Scheduler that has grown one method per incident (13 methods and counting); each growth required a fix commit to the protocol AND to the mirrored conformance-assertion blocks and fakes in at least three test files (_workflow_helpers.py:252-259, test_workflow_dry_run_hook.py:478-485, test_workflow_e2e.py:7467-7470). The underlying defect is that TaskWorkflow's seam to the scheduler is 'the whole Scheduler': status CRUD, task CRUD, train queries, requeue accounting, blast-radius handling, and MCP tool dispatch all flow through one ever-widening protocol, so every new workflow feature widens it again.
findings.proposal: Split the seam along its three real usage clusters and define each protocol next to its implementer in scheduler.py (so pyright checks Scheduler's conformance at the definition site, not at N test files): TaskStore (get_task/update_task/get_status/set_task_status/mark_done/dispatch_tool), TrainView (tasks_by_train/get_tasks/get_statuses), and RequeueAccounting (clear_requeue_count, handle_blast_radius_expansion). TaskWorkflow takes the three narrow deps; one canonical fake per facade lives in tests/_workflow_helpers.py. Drift then surfaces as a compile error in the commit that adds the dependency, not as a follow-up fix task.

clusters.hotspot: harness (orchestrator process-supervision, restart, watcher, and reconciliation-sweep layer)
clusters.architecture_notes: Harness (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/harness.py, 9,028 lines) is the god-module: its constructor wires ~78 instance attributes and its run() method is a ~650-line hand-numbered startup ritual (steps 0, 0a, 0a-post ... 1c0a2, 1c1c1 — the numbering itself shows accretion) followed by a finally-ladder shutdown of per-subsystem try/except blocks. It hosts ~11 hand-rolled background loops (merge worker, offline lane, orphan-L0 reaper, terminal-status watcher, watcher supervisor, stranded reconcile, main-tip sweep, no-landings breaker, deterministic-recon sweep, warm-lane GC, escalation server), each with its own _start/_stop/_loop triplet. Escalation-server callbacks arrive on FastMCP threadpool threads and are marshalled back via _schedule_coro_threadsafe (harness.py:7895). Task truth lives in five substrates — fused-memory status strings, git branch/ancestry, worktree directories, in-memory scheduler._dispatched/workflow dicts, and the escalation queue — and at least seven distinct sweeps independently re-derive consistency between them. Restart/self-restart logic is split three ways across service_restart.py (StaleServiceRestartCoordinator + schedule_detached_systemd_restart) and deterministic_runner.py (_default_schedule_detached_restart + blocking run+fresh-PID verify), each having independently re-discovered the same hardening (cwd, script absolutization, on-failure escalation, timeout kill). The DeterministicRunner deploy lifecycle is persisted as four write-once metadata stamps (before_done_ran_at / before_done_verified_at / gate_escalated_at / done_provenance) with no explicit state field; harness sweeps reverse-engineer runner state from that dict shape (_is_stranded_deterministic_shape, harness.py:380). Satellite stores (event_store.py, run_store.py, cost store) are small and share runs.db but each owns its own connect/schema/checkpoint logic. The Harness↔Scheduler seam is private monkey-patching: harness assigns nine scheduler._on_* callbacks and reads scheduler._dispatched / scheduler.lock_table._held directly.
clusters.cross_system_notes: Three concrete cross-subsystem compensation patterns. (1) fused-memory/Taskmaster provides no transactional guarantee that task status matches merge reality (no 'done iff merged' invariant, and set_task_status can be rejected or silently lost), so harness carries an entire git-archaeology layer to rebuild truth: _reconcile_one_stranded's merge-marker search, done_provenance conventions matched by string format to workflow.py:656 and consumed by fused-memory's _validate_done_provenance, plus SetTaskStatusRejected strike-counting with L1 escalation (harness.py:2889-2906). The missing upstream guarantee is an atomic status+provenance write with enforced legal transitions in fused-memory. (2) _pid_alive (harness.py:273-295) is an admitted behavioural duplicate of fused-memory/src/fused_memory/services/orchestrator_detector.py:58-72, copied 'without introducing a cross-package import edge' — the two liveness predicates can drift exactly like the systemctl-inspector twins did; a shared/ package helper (shared.proc_group already exists as precedent) is the right home. (3) The watcher-supervisor L2 machinery in harness (_WATCHER_ESCALATION_HEADERS lockstep contract, 11bd467996) exists to compensate for the escalation server originally lacking server-side level enforcement — the auto-watcher L1→L2 overstep class was only closed when the server grew level_forbidden (df 2041-2044); the header contract is still maintained 'in lockstep' by comment convention on the harness side.

findings.title: Four parallel restart/self-restart mechanisms, each independently re-hardened — no single process-supervision contract
findings.problem: The 'restart a service safely' job is implemented four times: (1) StaleServiceRestartCoordinator._default_restart_executor (service_restart.py:481-494, fire-and-forget start_new_session spawn, no verify), (2) schedule_detached_systemd_restart (service_restart.py:78-159, systemd-run transient unit — its own docstring at :89-102 admits it mirrors the runner's argv pattern 'but WITHOUT its /bin/sh on-failure escalation wrapper — an accepted gap', and it passes no --working-directory), (3) DeterministicRunner._default_schedule_detached_restart (deterministic_runner.py:249-383, has --working-directory + cwd absolutization + on-failure escalation — added only after task 2105's exit-127 bug), and (4) DeterministicRunner's blocking cross-unit run + fresh-PID verify (deterministic_runner.py:448+, 1196+). Each path re-discovered a different subset of the invariants (absolute script path, explicit cwd, own-unit detection, escalate-on-fire-time-failure, verify-by-fresh-PID, timeout+group-kill). Own-unit detection (deterministic_runner.py:240-247) fails OPEN to the cross-unit blocking path when ORCH_UNIT is unset — which is the self-kill path (task 2064 fleet incident).
findings.proposal: Create orchestrator/proc_supervision.py with a single RestartPlan dataclass {script: absolute Path, args, cwd: required, target_unit, own_unit, on_failure_escalation: EscalationSpec|None, verify: FreshPidVerify|None} and one execute() that (a) derives detached-vs-blocking from own-unit comparison, (b) FAILS CLOSED when target==unknown-own-unit (refuse + escalate instead of blocking self-kill), (c) always sets --working-directory and absolutizes the script, (d) always wraps detached payloads with the on-failure escalation shell, (e) always runs fresh-PID verify against a persisted baseline for blocking restarts. service_restart.schedule_detached_systemd_restart and DeterministicRunner._default_schedule_detached_restart both become thin callers; the 'accepted gap' dies. Any future restart caller inherits all five invariants for free.

findings.title: DeterministicRunner deploy lifecycle is an implicit state machine of four scattered metadata stamps with no legal-transition enforcement
findings.problem: Deploy progress is persisted as independent write-once dict keys in task metadata (before_done_ran_at, before_done_verified_at, gate_escalated_at, done_provenance) with the legal states only implicit in code. Every crash window between two stamps invented a new undefined state: 1900's phantom-done (ran_at set, nothing else → resume drove straight to done), 2059's silent strand, 2066's lost terminal writeback. The harness recon sweep must reverse-engineer runner state from the raw dict shape via _is_stranded_deterministic_shape (harness.py:380-407) — runner-internal knowledge duplicated across module boundary. Worse, the fresh-PID verify baseline (ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic) is a local variable never persisted, so retroactive verification is provably impossible — harness.py:322-341 documents this at length and settles for a 'near-constant healthy' liveness check that cannot distinguish 'deploy took effect' from 'unit was already up'.
findings.proposal: Define a DeployState schema module (e.g. orchestrator/deploy_state.py): a typed dataclass with from_metadata()/to_metadata(), a single metadata.deploy_state phase enum (scheduled → ran → verified|failed|escalated → done) plus a persisted verify baseline field, and a transition table enforced at every write (illegal transition → loud escalation, never silent). DeterministicRunner writes phase+stamp atomically in one update_task call; harness sweeps and the resume path branch on the explicit phase instead of stamp-combination archaeology. This makes every crash window land in a NAMED state with a defined recovery action, and makes post-hoc freshness verification possible (persisted baseline vs live ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic).
findings.bug_history_link: task 1900 3c3cbd13cd (crash-window phantom-done, fixed by requiring positive-proof stamps), task 2059 strand + task 2074 recon sweep (Source A/B recovery, _deterministic_deploy_health_verdict CAVEAT about unpersisted baseline), task 2066 (writeback retries + durable escalation on budget exhaustion), ad436389c6 (resume guard hardening) — the mined '5x DeterministicRunner resume/crash-window correctness' theme

findings.title: Duplicated systemctl inspector diverged: harness copy lacks the task-2091 timeout guard — latent sweep-loop hang
findings.problem: _recon_inspect_unit (harness.py:351-377) is an admitted 'standalone duplicate of DeterministicRunner._default_inspect_unit' (its own docstring, :354-357), copied because the runner's inspector is a private bound method. The twins have already diverged: after task 2091, the runner's version wraps proc.communicate() in asyncio.wait_for(timeout=self._inspect_timeout_secs) with kill+bounded-reap (deterministic_runner.py:398-434); the harness copy still does a bare `stdout, _ = await proc.communicate()` at harness.py:366. A wedged `systemctl --user show` (the exact 2087/2091 signature: systemd busy, or a grandchild inheriting the stdout pipe) will hang _run_deterministic_recon_sweep — and since the sweep loop awaits the pass, the deterministic-strand recovery subsystem silently stops forever.
findings.proposal: Hoist the inspector to one module-level function inspect_systemd_unit(unit: str, *, timeout_secs: float) -> dict in the new proc_supervision.py (or a shared systemd helper), containing the wait_for + kill + sentinel-return hardening exactly once. DeterministicRunner._default_inspect_unit and harness._recon_inspect_unit both delegate to it (the runner keeps its injectable seam). Also fold _deterministic_deploy_health_verdict next to it so verdict semantics live beside the data they classify.

findings.title: Eleven hand-rolled background-loop triplets + a comment-ordered startup/shutdown ritual — the source of the recurring shutdown-hang class
findings.problem: Harness has 11 _start_X/_stop_X/_X_loop triplets (harness.py:4439/4461, 4535/4560, 6069/6166, 6262/6306, 6488/6677, 6686/6712, 6886/6910, 6935/6973, 7370/7395, 7418/7442, 7820/7845), each hand-rolling the same idempotent-start check, cancel+suppress stop, and CancelledError-re-raise/log/backoff loop body — with subtle per-copy variations (the watcher supervisor loop alone, harness.py:7049-7230, carries four nested try/except layers, two counters and two deques added across tasks 1388/1430/1443/1449). run()'s startup is a ~20-step sequence whose ordering constraints exist only in prose comments (step labels 0..1c1g, with 1c1c1 ordered before 1c1c), and shutdown is a finally-ladder of per-subsystem try/except (harness.py:1618+) whose ordering (cancel workflows BEFORE usage_gate.shutdown, checkpoint stores while loop healthy) is again comment-enforced. This structure is exactly why shutdown correctness took 5+ passes and why cli.py needs a daemon-thread os._exit(137) watchdog as a backstop.
findings.proposal: Introduce a BackgroundService/LifecycleRegistry abstraction: a small class per loop (name, interval/backoff policy, single async pass_fn, failure-log bounding) plus a registry the Harness populates in declared order — registry.start_all() starts in order, registry.stop_all() cancels in reverse with a per-service timeout and one uniform CancelledError contract. The 11 triplets collapse to registrations; run()'s finally collapses to one stop_all() call; the os._exit watchdog remains as last resort but the hang class (one loop swallowing CancelledError or one stop call wedging the ladder) becomes structurally impossible. Task 1907's 'bound background-loop failure logging' fix becomes a property of the class, not of each copy.
findings.bug_history_link: mined '5x graceful shutdown/SIGTERM hang' theme (tasks 108, 161/162/169, 875 'hangs in asyncio cleanup after SIGTERM — never exits', 1080 '45s os._exit timer leaks into pytest'), ad69a8d093 (1907: bound background-loop failure logging), watcher-loop fix chain 1388/1430/1443/1449

findings.title: Task ground truth re-derived independently by seven sweeps across five state substrates — every new crash shape spawns a new sweep
findings.problem: A task's true state is spread over five substrates (fused-memory status string, git branch existence/ancestry/merge-marker, worktree directory, in-memory scheduler._dispatched + workflow dict, escalation queue), and no single component owns the mapping. Consequently harness accreted at least seven reconciliation sweeps that each re-implement parts of the derivation: _recover_crashed_tasks (:1932), _reconcile_stranded_in_progress (:2779, with R3 cancel-grace and R4 blocked-status guards bolted on), _reconcile_one_stranded (:2964, is_ancestor fast-path + branch-deleted merge-marker archaeology + degenerate-branch check), _revert_in_progress_if_no_live_claimant (:3399), _scan_for_terminal_active_tasks (:7288), _run_main_tip_sweep (:7483), and _run_deterministic_recon_sweep (:7738, which needed explicit Source-A/Source-B within-pass mutual exclusion, c6f72ec25e). Each sweep has its own dedup counters (_reconcile_failure_counts), race guards, and status whitelists (_RECONCILE_SWEEP_STATUSES) that can disagree; the 7x fix theme shows the same state machine kept producing new stuck-task shapes (stuck-done, degenerate-branch, stranded-in-progress, stranded-blocked, out-of-band-merged-blocked).
findings.proposal: Extract a TaskGroundTruth resolver module: one async derive_truth(tid) -> TruthReport{db_status, live_claimant(plan.lock/owner_pid), branch_state ∈ {on_main(sha), exists_off_main, gone_with_merge_marker(sha), gone_no_marker}, worktree_present, open_escalations} plus ONE classification table mapping TruthReport → recovery action (mark_done_with_provenance / revert_to_pending / re_file_escalation / leave). All sweeps become thin schedulers over this shared derivation; the is_ancestor→rev-parse→find_merge_marker archaeology and the done_provenance convention exist exactly once. New crash shapes then require adding a table row, not a new 400-line sweep with fresh race guards.

findings.title: Harness↔Scheduler seam is private monkey-patching: nine _on_* callback assignments plus direct reads of scheduler internals
findings.problem: Harness.__init__ wires the scheduler by assigning private attributes: scheduler._on_park_stop_trip, _on_external_dep_block, _on_starvation_warn/_resolve, _warm_base_health_probe, _on_warm_base_warn/_promote_l2/_resolve, _suppress_blocked_write (harness.py:774-810), and later writes scheduler._module_cache[task_id] directly (:1923). The mid-run stranded sweep reads scheduler._dispatched and scheduler.lock_table._held (harness.py:2865-2868) to decide whether a task is 'actively held' — a liveness judgment duplicated outside the single writer of that state. There is no declared interface, so (a) the dispatch-vs-sweep race had to be patched with the R3 cancel-grace window and dispatched/held filters after stranded tasks were reverted out from under live workflows, and (b) tests must mock privates, producing the fixture-drift failures that forced the supervisor loop to deliberately re-raise AttributeError (harness.py:7087-7095, task 1449).
findings.proposal: Define a SchedulerCallbacks protocol (dataclass of the nine hooks) accepted by Scheduler's constructor, and add public accessors scheduler.is_actively_held(tid) and scheduler.cache_modules(tid, modules) so _dispatched/lock_table stay single-writer with the holding judgment computed where the state lives (including the cancel-grace semantics, which currently live in harness's _workflow_cancel_recent). This turns the sweep-vs-dispatch race from a comment-guarded convention into an API guarantee and lets tests fake one protocol instead of nine private attributes.

clusters.architecture_notes: GitOps (git_ops.py, 6.8k lines, ~130 methods on one class) owns every git-touching lifecycle: task worktrees, the warm-lane pool, the merge-spec lane pool, persistent merge/offline-deep worktrees, interactive worktrees, train stacking, main advancement, and red-main recovery. WarmLanePool (warm_lane_pool.py) is deliberately a pure in-memory FREE/ASSIGNED two-state machine plus a branch→lane assignment map under one asyncio.Lock — but the REAL lane lifecycle (seeded/registered/attached-to-branch/carrying-plan/identity-bound) is not modeled anywhere; it is re-derived at every decision point from five independent sources: (1) pool in-memory state, (2) git's .git/worktrees admin registration, (3) the lane dir + .task/plan.json sidecar inside the tree, (4) the task/<id> branch ref and its commits-beyond-main, (5) the .pool-root mount sentinel. acquire_warm_lane (lines 2502-3065) is a 565-line runtime reconciler over the cross-product of those sources with seven distinct routes (in-memory reuse, disk-backstop reuse, identity-mismatch reset, create-once fresh, create-once reattach, reset-in-place reattach, fresh recycle), each with its own fault/teardown idiom. Harness is a second writer to pool state via restore_assignment/note_assignment/drop_assignment (crash recovery at harness.py:1932-2270 and _reconcile_lane_checkouts at 2273+), so lifecycle ownership is split across two modules. Pool storage health is a sentinel-file protocol (.pool-root) with one writer buried in _seed_warm_lane and ~6 guard readers, each needing its own bootstrap escape. worktree_identity.py is a small clean seam (title-based recycled-id guard). offline_lane.py is a self-contained worker with its own file lock. cargo_scope.py is unrelated verify-scoping and healthy.
clusters.cross_system_notes: Three clear cases of this subsystem patching around missing guarantees elsewhere. (1) reify's shell-script substrate: warm-lane seeding, disk-guard, and GC live in reify's repo (seed-warm-lane.sh, warm-lane-disk-guard.sh, warm-lane-gc.sh); git_ops encodes their absence as fail-open rc=127 sentinels and — critically — delegates a LOCK-SAFETY invariant to them: the comment at git_ops.py:2619-2629 states the disk-guard/reclaim runs without the pool lock and 'the safety invariant is delegated to the γ/δ scripts: warm-lane-gc.sh MUST only reset lanes idle beyond a threshold... δ must skip ASSIGNED lanes' — an unenforced cross-repo contract documented as a message to a future script author. (2) fused-memory/Taskmaster task-id recycling: the entire worktree_identity.py module + the identity guards in acquire_warm_lane (2710-2724, 2957-2963) and _recover_crashed_tasks (harness.py:2090-2128) exist solely because the task registry re-mints deleted ids onto unrelated work (reify task 3770) — the upstream missing guarantee is monotonic, never-recycled task ids; enforcing that in fused-memory's submit_task would let the whole title-matching heuristic (with its documented fail-open false-negative window) be deleted. (3) LLM-agent behavior: the six-layer .task/ defense exists because agents 'bypass them routinely' (git_ops.py:24) — the sandbox/agent harness provides no guarantee about which git commands agents run, so git_ops absorbs it with scrubs; relocating .task/ out-of-tree (finding 4) is the structural fix. Conversely, defects HERE drove patching elsewhere: the reconciler (fused-memory side) grew a degenerate-branch-ref skip (task 2112, cf43710926) to tolerate zero-commit task/<id> refs leaked by acquire_warm_lane seed-faults, and CLAUDE.md operator memory shows repeated human /unblock protocols built around the acquire-fault and citation-missing symptom classes.

findings.title: git worktree prune has 6 unguarded call sites bypassing the 2099 registration-wipe guard
findings.problem: The Jul-3/4 incident (orphan-reaper ran `git worktree prune` over an unmounted lane mount and wiped ALL lane registrations, then reuse fast-path + restore_assignment re-poisoned lanes on every requeue) was fixed by task 2099 with a pool_storage_present() refuse-gate — but that gate lives ONLY inside prune_worktrees() (git_ops.py:6758-6812). Five other raw `_run(['git','worktree','prune'])` sites bypass it entirely: create_worktree leftover-branch cleanup (git_ops.py:3824), materialize_member_solo (4341), delete_solo_branch (4426), prune_stale_merge_worktrees (5365), reap_interactive_worktrees (5725), plus the harness substrate-gate cleanup (harness.py:4765). The merge-lane sites (4341/4426/5365) run on merge-queue activity independent of lane-pool health, so during the exact mount-down window 2099 guards against, a train-stacking or solo-branch cleanup can still wipe every mount-resident lane's admin entry — recreating the CRITICAL incident through a side door.
findings.proposal: Create one chokepoint: GitOps._prune_registrations(context: str) that (a) refuses when pool_in_use() and not pool_storage_present() (firing _note_pool_storage_absent), (b) is the ONLY place the literal ['git','worktree','prune'] argv may appear. findings.title: Catch-all fault path in acquire_warm_lane still uses bare pool.release, re-creating the task-2062 stale-checkout collision
findings.problem: acquire_warm_lane has four divergent teardown idioms: release_warm_lane (detach HEAD + branch-retention + pool release; lines 2751, 2803, and via _reset_and_seed_recycled_lane at 3320/3348 — the task-2062 fix sites), `git worktree remove --force` + bare pool.release (2870-2874, 2912-2916), degenerate-ref delete on exactly one of those paths (2936), and the top-level `except Exception` handler at 3060-3065 which does a bare `self.warm_lane_pool.release(lane)` with NO HEAD detach. findings.title: Warm-lane lifecycle has no authoritative durable state — five derivable sources reconciled ad hoc at every decision point
findings.problem: The lane lifecycle (seed -> registered -> assigned -> in-use -> released) is NOT an enforced state machine with a single owner. WarmLanePool models only FREE/ASSIGNED in memory (warm_lane_pool.py:18-21) and is mutated by TWO modules: GitOps acquire/release paths and Harness recovery (restore_assignment at harness.py:2189/2397/2418/2434, note_assignment at git_ops.py:2966). Everything else — registration, branch attachment, occupant identity — is re-derived per call from git admin dirs, .task/plan.json, branch refs, and the mount sentinel. acquire_warm_lane (2502-3065) and _recover_crashed_tasks (harness.py:1932-2270) are both giant decision trees over the cross-product of these sources, and each historical bug is one unhandled cell: orphaned registration with surviving assignment (task 2097), stale plan.json re-pinning a broken lane (task 2098/reify 4655/4947), detached-HEAD stale branch ref (task 1923 residual at git_ops.py:3097-3116), recycled-id identity adoption (reify 3770 -> worktree_identity.py), previous occupant's .task/ inherited on reattach (reify esc-4920-163 -> the rmtree at git_ops.py:3030). Derived state silently diverges by design because nothing records what state a lane is SUPPOSED to be in.
findings.proposal: Add a durable per-lane record written transactionally at every transition: <worktree_base>/.lane-state/<lane-name>.json holding {state, task_id, title, branch, seeded_from_sha, updated_at} (lives ON the pool mount, so it vanishes with the mount — coherent with the 2099 sentinel logic). Wrap it in a LaneLifecycle class that is the SINGLE writer for both the in-memory pool and the record, with an explicit legal-transition table (assert on illegal transitions, escalate instead of heal). Startup recovery then becomes: read record, verify git reality matches, quarantine on divergence — replacing the heuristic adopt/clean/re-pin tree in _recover_crashed_tasks. The disk-backstop plan.json probe, note_assignment/restore_assignment split, and the identity title guard all collapse into record-vs-DB comparison in one place.

findings.title: .task/ sidecar lives inside the git worktree — one leak class defended by six redundant guards instead of removed
findings.problem: Task metadata (.task/plan.json, iterations.jsonl, reviews/, agent_session.json) is stored INSIDE the worktree that hostile-by-accident LLM agents run arbitrary git commands in. The module docstring (git_ops.py:3-24) openly catalogs SIX belt-and-braces guards: scrub_task_dir_from_tree (244+, called at warm-lane acquire 3044, merges, worktree create), _assert_no_task_dir before advance_main, create_worktree inherited-contamination scrub, commit()'s :!.task pathspec PLUS post-staging unstage net (3859-3878, 'agents bypass them routinely'), merge_to_main post-merge scrub, plus .gitignore layers (artifacts.py:183-196) — and STILL new cells appear: the occupant-switch rmtree at git_ops.py:3030 (reify esc-4920-163 cross-task contamination) and four :!.task/ pathspec exclusions in merge_gates.py (1087, 1117, 1261, 1282). The mined fix history shows 5+ separate hardening rounds for this ONE class. The structural cause is the location: any in-tree path can be staged by an agent, and any checkout/clean/reset interacts with it, so every new git operation needs a new guard forever.
findings.proposal: Move task artifacts out of the git tree: <worktree_base>/.task-meta/<worktree-name>/ (sibling pattern already proven by quarantine_base, git_ops.py:6676-6681), with artifacts.py TaskArtifacts as the single path-derivation owner and the path handed to agents/mcp_lifecycle via config. Then the entire defense layer — scrub functions, pathspec exclusions, post-staging nets, per-incident rmtrees, .task/.gitignore writers — becomes dead code, and contamination of main becomes structurally impossible rather than 6x-guarded. Bonus: lane identity metadata survives `git clean -xfd`/`checkout -f`, simplifying the reuse/identity guards too. Keep _assert_no_task_dir as a cheap tripwire during migration.

findings.title: Pool-storage presence is a scattered sentinel protocol with one hidden writer and duplicated bootstrap escapes
findings.problem: The .pool-root mount-health protocol is smeared across the codebase: the ONLY writer is _seed_warm_lane on rc==0 (documented at git_ops.py:963-965), while readers each hand-roll the guard + bootstrap escape: acquire_warm_lane create-once (2778-2804) and acquire_spec_lane create-once (2302-2326) duplicate the same ~25-line 'exists && !present -> bootstrap_ok? mark : refuse' block verbatim; prune_worktrees (6780-6805), _run_warm_lane_gc_reclaim, and harness crash recovery (1959-1967) each carry their own variant plus the pool_in_use() pre-gate added in step-16 because pool-less hosts were misread as mount-down. The writer/reader coupling, the bootstrap escape, and the pool-less-host exemption get one unit-tested implementation instead of N copies that must be co-evolved (2099 needed a same-day review-fix + two amendments because they weren't).

clusters.architecture_notes: The scheduler subsystem is one 4.7k-line module containing an exception taxonomy for fused-memory rejections, MCP response parsing, ModuleLockTable (hierarchical locks + LIFO park stacks), and the Scheduler class, which is simultaneously the fused-memory task client (get_tasks/set_task_status/update_task with retry/rejection classification), the dispatch-policy engine, and four watchdogs (external-dep, starvation, warm-base hard-down, park-stop circuit breaker). Dispatch eligibility IS now centralized in one pure predicate (_eligible_for_dispatch → _deps_satisfied, scheduler.py:2764/2534) used by both the pin loop and the scored loop — the 1026/1028-era duplication was genuinely fixed — but the side-effecting policy passes that must agree with it (_apply_external_dep_policy, _park_gc, _owner_is_live_dispatchable) are separate hand-synchronized re-derivations. Core state is ~15 process-local per-task dicts/sets (_dispatched, _skip_count, _requeue_until, _last_dispatch_at, _module_cache, five external-dep counters, starvation pair, park-stop deque+set), each with bespoke reset semantics and a manually-enumerated per-tick GC sweep inside the 720-line acquire_next tick; phase ordering invariants live only in comments. Durable state lives in three SQLite stores (OverrideStore, ParkEvictionRequestStore, run_store snapshot) plus task metadata in fused-memory. The task-status lifecycle is NOT a state machine anywhere: task_status.py is three frozensets, the scheduler dispatches only 'pending', and every other transition is written by workflow/steward/escalation-server/reconciliation/DeterministicRunner through set_task_status with only spot server-side gates (terminal-exit, done-gate, provenance). Dead-end states (in-progress-with-no-claimant, blocked-after-external-dep-escalation) are recovered by the harness's heuristic reconcile sweep (harness.py:2780+), which infers claimant liveness from plan.lock/pid and infers merged-ness by grepping main commit subjects. DeterministicRunner.run (deterministic_runner.py:838-1368) is a persisted state machine encoded as presence/absence of metadata stamps plus escalation-queue archive scans. The Harness reaches into Scheduler privates extensively (installs 8 callbacks on _on_* attrs, writes _module_cache, reads _dispatched/_held/_requeue_history), so the real Scheduler API is an unnamed, unversioned surface.
clusters.cross_system_notes: Three clear cases. (1) The harness stranded-task reconcile sweep (harness.py:2780-3400) exists because the merge queue / workflow provide no durable task→merged record: after advance_main + branch cleanup, done-ness must be re-inferred via `git merge-base --is-ancestor` and find_merge_marker's grep of main commit subjects for 'Merge {branch} into {main}' — a missing write-side guarantee in the merge subsystem patched with read-side forensics in the harness/scheduler seam. (2) The escalation server's resolve_issue(action='resume') contract 'stays in-progress' (escalation/src/escalation/server.py:521) assumes a live L0 workflow; for memberless/stranded cases it strands tasks in a status the scheduler never dispatches (scheduler.py:2805 gates on 'pending'), which the harness sweep then compensates for — the documented esc-2073-15 incident class. (3) scheduler.set_task_status carries an action-teardown suppression predicate (_suppress_blocked_write, scheduler.py:1586-1603) purely to absorb racing 'blocked' writes from workflows being killed — the scheduler patching for the workflow subsystem's lack of write fencing on teardown. Additionally the _TRANSIENT_RETRIES loop in set_task_status compensates for fused-memory's taskmaster-child restart window.

findings.title: DeterministicRunner proves 'human resolved the deploy' by task-scoped escalation existence — any unrelated escalation aliases as resolution proof
findings.problem: DeterministicRunner.run reconstructs its persisted state from stamp-presence combinatorics (gate_escalated_at, before_done_ran_at, before_done_verified_at, before_done_scheduled_at) plus escalation-queue scans keyed ONLY by task_id. deterministic_runner.py:952 sets ever_escalated = bool(self.escalation_queue.get_by_task(task_id)) with no agent_role/category filter and archive included (queue.py:309-326 scans archive when status=None); branch (b) at :1013-1029 then drives the task to done with note 'resumed after human resolution'. But the starvation watchdog files escalations with the same task_id into the same queue (harness.py:3940-3990, agent_role='orchestrator-starvation-watchdog'), and gate escalations from the task's own earlier life also persist in the archive. Similarly the section-1 quiescence check at :861 blocks on ANY pending escalation for the task, not just the runner's own gate.
findings.proposal: Replace stamp-combinatorics with one explicit persisted state field: metadata.deterministic_state = {state: enum(created|action_stamped|action_verified|scheduled|gate_filed|failed_escalated|done), evidence: {...}} written atomically via update_task(metadata_mode='merge') as a single key, with a legal-transition table in DeterministicRunner (module-level dict, assert on every write). Scope all escalation queries with the runner's sentinel agent_role ('orchestrator-deterministic') — add an agent_role filter parameter to EscalationQueue.get_by_task and use it at deterministic_runner.py:861, :922 and :952. The 'ever_escalated' inference dies entirely: resolution proof becomes state==failed_escalated + that specific escalation's resolved record.

The ever_escalated aliasing itself is a confirmed-by-reading residual phantom-done vector of the same class 3c1900 tried to close.

findings.title: Task-status lifecycle has no transition authority; dead-end states are recovered by heuristic compensation sweeps in another subsystem
findings.problem: task_status.py:11-44 is three frozensets — there is no (from_status, to_status, actor) legality table anywhere. The scheduler dispatches only 'pending' (scheduler.py:2805); the escalation server's resume action leaves tasks 'in-progress' by contract (escalation/server.py:521 'stays in-progress'), a status nothing re-dispatches; the external-dep policy blocks tasks and documents 'blocked tasks are not re-evaluated automatically — manually set back to pending' (scheduler.py:1962-1969, 2124-2126). Recovery of these dead ends is delegated to the harness's periodic stranded-sweep (harness.py:97 _RECONCILE_SWEEP_STATUSES, :2780-3400), which infers claimant liveness from plan.lock/owner_pid and infers merged-ness by grepping main's commit subjects (find_merge_marker). Server-side enforcement exists only as spot gates (terminal-exit, done-gate, provenance — scheduler.py:1622-1690 handles their rejections).
findings.proposal: Add a TaskLifecycle transition table enforced at the single write chokepoint that already exists (fused-memory TaskInterceptor, which already gates terminal-exit): a dict of (from, to, actor_class) → allowed, where actor_class comes from the existing agent_id tagging. Make 'claimant' a first-class task field (run_id + heartbeat timestamp, stamped at dispatch, cleared at release) so 'stranded' becomes a queryable predicate instead of plan.lock/pid forensics. Change resume semantics to blocked→pending when no live claimant (the exact esc-2073-15 fix, but enforced structurally). The harness sweep shrinks to 'claimant heartbeat expired → pending', and find_merge_marker dies once the merge queue durably records task→merged-sha before branch cleanup.
findings.bug_history_link: esc-2073-15 / feedback memory 'stranded_blocked resume leaves task in-progress' (2026-07-04); task 52 'Scheduler dispatches tasks with in-progress dependencies'; harness 'Fix 4: stuck-blocked recovery' and 'R4: sweep blocked for out-of-band merges' comments (harness.py:2798, 2858); external-dep arc tasks 1854/1855/1799 all include 'manually re-pend' remediation text; C3.2/task 1620 _suppress_blocked_write patch for racing teardown writes.

findings.title: Module-lock derivation from metadata.files duplicated at 4+ sites with the lock-charter strip re-implemented per site, plus a dual-writer module cache
findings.problem: The pipeline strip_directory_locks → files_to_modules(depth) is independently coded in Scheduler._get_modules (scheduler.py:4726-4742), Harness._tag_task_modules (harness.py:1901-1923, which also writes scheduler._module_cache directly), Scheduler._persist_files_metadata (scheduler.py:4316), and handle_blast_radius_expansion (writes _module_cache at :4456). The 54ec90fefc commit message documents the exact failure: the strip was added to the read path but a write site (module-tagger writeback) missed it, so the fused-memory lock-charter guard rejected the ENTIRE payload and silently dropped valid file entries. _module_cache has two writers (harness startup + blast-radius) while _get_modules itself never populates it after deriving (:4742 returns without caching) — cached and derived values can diverge after a metadata update.
findings.proposal: Create module_charter.py owning: derive_modules(files, depth) -> list[str] (strip + files_to_modules + diagnostics), and sanitize_files_for_persist(files) -> list[str] used by every metadata.files write path. Make _module_cache single-writer: only _get_modules populates it (write-through on derive), harness seeds via a public Scheduler.seed_modules(task_id, files) that routes through the same function. The lock-charter file-shape rule (Contract 1: file-level always, coarsen at read) then has exactly one implementation on each side of the wire.
findings.bug_history_link: 54ec80/54ec90fefc 'strip directory entries in module-tagger writeback' (esc-1905-31), b0acbd7684 'fix update_task structured-rejection nesting bug' (1905 step-10), 8e94d0fdc5 'persist file-level paths in _persist_files_metadata', lock-charter Contract-1 decision (task 1905); reify-3468 subtree-lock incident cited at scheduler.py:4728.

findings.title: Five+ hand-rolled consecutive-tick streak counters, each with bespoke reset/GC, manually enumerated in the per-tick stale-id sweep
findings.problem: The 'N consecutive ticks then fire, reset on clean tick, GC on terminal' pattern is implemented five separate times with subtly different semantics: _external_unresolved_counts (scheduler.py:2104-2153), _external_resolver_degraded_counts (:2001-2060), _external_hold_streak/_external_hold_cause (:1898-1937, cause-change reset), _local_backfill_unresolved_counts (three near-identical inline nested loops in acquire_next :3396-3488, one per degradation mode), and _starvation_first_seen/_starvation_escalated (:2179+). The acquire_next stale-id GC sweep (:3552-3633) must manually enumerate every dict, with dedicated comment-documented carve-outs ('sweep separately to avoid mutating while iterating', 'uses a SEPARATE guard... so it runs even when those dicts are empty'). Every new watchdog re-litigates reset-on-recovery and leak-on-terminal by hand.
findings.proposal: Introduce a StreakCounter/BookkeepingRegistry class: register(name, key_fn, threshold, on_fire) with touch(key)/clear(key)/gc(stale_ids) methods; the tick GC becomes registry.gc(stale_ids) over all registered counters, and 'reset streak on clean tick' / 'cause-change resets streak' become constructor options instead of re-derived logic. The three duplicated backfill-degradation loops in acquire_next collapse into one helper taking the missing-dep set. This structurally prevents the leak-and-drift class (counter must equal derived reality but can drift after recover→degrade gaps or terminal-before-threshold exits).
