findings.title: Substrate-probe predicate duplicated with divergent semantics — malformed probe fails OPEN at the real dispatch gate
findings.problem: Two same-named predicates disagree: substrate_gate.carries_substrate_probe (substrate_gate.py:81-112) is True whenever the substrate_probe KEY exists — written specifically so run_substrate_recheck fails CLOSED (verdict=FLIP) on a declared-but-malformed descriptor (:265-280). Scheduler.carries_substrate_probe (scheduler.py:1412-1428) instead returns extract_probe_set(task) is not None, which is False for a malformed/empty descriptor. The production gate at harness.py:5108 uses the Scheduler version to decide whether to run the recheck at all — so a task whose substrate_probe descriptor is malformed (non-dict, or missing/empty probe_set, e.g. after a metadata-shape drift like the c20c69b28c/a083114d00 class) silently SKIPS the substrate gate entirely; the fail-closed branch in run_substrate_recheck is unreachable.
findings.proposal: Delete Scheduler.carries_substrate_probe. Harness:5108 should call substrate_gate.carries_substrate_probe (key-presence) and let run_substrate_recheck's own SKIP/FLIP logic decide policy — the module already encodes the fail-closed invariant correctly, the wrapper defeated it. Add a test asserting a task with substrate_probe='garbage' produces FLIP (blocked dispatch), not a skipped gate. This also matches the stated intent in the Scheduler docstring ('single source of truth') by making the substrate_gate version the actual single source.
findings.bug_history_link: Speculative as an incident, but it is a textbook instance of the mined 6x theme 'caller sends a shape the write path doesn't expect' (c20c69b28c update_task dict-or-string, a083114d00 reopen_reason coercion, b0acbd7684 structured-rejection nesting) — metadata-shape drift is the documented normal failure mode, and this gate fails open under exactly that drift.

findings.title: Harness drives Scheduler through private state: 8 callback installs, cache writes, and _dispatched/_held reads form an unnamed contract whose ordering invariants live in comments
findings.problem: Harness installs eight callbacks onto private Scheduler attributes post-construction (harness.py:774-810: _on_park_stop_trip, _on_external_dep_block, _on_starvation_warn/_resolve, _warm_base_health_probe, _on_warm_base_warn/_promote_l2/_resolve, _suppress_blocked_write), writes scheduler._module_cache (:1923), reads scheduler._dispatched at 6+ sites (:2544, :2701, :2754, :2866) and lock_table._held (:2867) as liveness oracles, and reads _requeue_history (:5820). Correctness depends on startup ordering documented only in comments ('runs while scheduler._dispatched is still empty' at :1408/:1418/:1422/:2453/:2789) — nothing enforces that the orphan reaper and stranded sweep actually run before the first acquire_next. Scheduler.release itself reaches into lock_table._held (scheduler.py:4490). Every new watchdog adds another private-attr pair, growing the god-module in both files.
findings.proposal: Make the seam explicit: (1) a SchedulerCallbacks frozen dataclass passed to Scheduler.__init__ (all _on_* hooks become constructor state — no post-hoc mutation, no half-wired window); (2) public read API is_dispatched(task_id) / holds_lock(task_id) / requeue_history(task_id) replacing the _dispatched/_held/_requeue_history reach-ins; (3) a Scheduler.seed_modules() for the cache write (see module-charter finding); (4) an explicit started flag asserting acquire_next is not called before Harness.finish_startup(), turning the comment-only ordering invariant into a runtime check.
findings.bug_history_link: The mid_run filter at harness.py:2866-2868 exists because the sweep once raced live workflows via exactly this shared-private access; task 1620 C3.2 _suppress_blocked_write and its 'MUST sit BEFORE dispatch_tool' placement note (scheduler.py:1586-1593) show the callback seam already produced a placement bug class; bc7ae6f303 'expose Scheduler.override_store' is a prior instance of retrofitting a public alias onto this private surface.

findings.title: acquire_next is a 720-line tick with 10+ ordered side-effecting phases whose sequencing constraints exist only as prose
findings.problem: acquire_next (scheduler.py:3305-4026) inlines: warm-base watchdog, active fetch, dep-status backfill (with three duplicated degradation loops), park-eviction drain (which must run BEFORE park-GC 'so the operator audit event wins' :3490-3493), park-GC, a five-dict stale-id sweep, cooldown GC (must run 'before both candidate loops' :3635-3640), external-dep policy pass (exactly-once-per-tick invariant :3642-3677), override GC + reserve-now short-circuit with pre/post-snapshot diff bookkeeping (:3707-3808), starvation pass, pin loop, and scored loop. Each ordering constraint is enforced by nothing but position and comment; several historical fixes were pure reordering/scoping of these phases. The method also mixes pure selection with persistence (snapshot writes at three exits).
findings.proposal: Decompose the tick into an explicit pipeline: a TickContext dataclass (tasks, status_map, tasks_by_id, external_cache, overrides, candidates) built once, and an ordered list of phase objects (Hygiene: evictions→park_gc→stale_sweep→cooldown_gc; Policy: external_dep→starvation; Selection: pins→scored) where each phase declares what it reads/writes on the context. Ordering becomes data (a list literal) that a unit test can assert against, phase-level tests stop needing a full acquire_next harness, and the three duplicated backfill loops merge inside one Backfill phase. Split along the real seams only — the lock table and selection scoring already have clean boundaries; do not split the file for line count alone.

clusters.architecture_notes: verify.py (3.6k lines) is the god-module: it owns (1) scope derivation — which test/lint/type commands to run for a diff (scope_module_config, _build_fallback_config, _apply_cargo_scope, plus a chain of shell-string rewriters _scope_command/_strip_directory_flag/_strip_leading_cd/_reproject_bare_uv_run/_force_serial_pytest/_maybe_govern_merge_cmd); (2) execution (run_verification's retry loop over three parallel (rc,out,timed_out,started_at,duration) scalar tuples, _run_cmd with cgroup-scope and clock-stop options); (3) failure classification (a single tool-agnostic regex ladder _classify_failure/_extract_cause_hint producing a stringly-typed category); (4) log persistence + a throttled archive pruner with module-global state (_LAST_PRUNE_AT); and (5) two copy-pasted ephemeral-worktree probes (verify_failure_is_preexisting_on_main, run_main_tip_sweep). Orchestration entry is run_scoped_verification, which computes the scope decision inline and interleaved with execution — there is no separable 'plan' object; scoping decisions are only observable as log lines. verify_runner.py is the multi-host seam: MergeVerifySpec (frozen dataclass + canonical JSON codec) ships UNSCOPED per-module commands + task_files to a runner host, which re-derives scope by re-entering run_scoped_verification — so scope derivation itself is not duplicated across hosts, only deferred. merge_gates.py consumes verify via the unscoped-typecheck Decision-3 gate and sentinel categories (UNSCOPED_TYPECHECK_*). b3_gate.py is a dependency-light CLI that gates autonomous low-risk unblocks by reading metadata.dry_run_proposals straight out of tasks.db sqlite JSON and string-prefix-matching block_reason. Key cross-module state: VerifyResult.category strings are branched on in workflow.py, merge_queue.py, and harness.py; the category taxonomy lives in 5+ manually-synced registries. offline_lane does NOT duplicate scope logic — it shells out to committed project scripts (clean seam).
clusters.cross_system_notes: Three clear cases of verify patching around missing guarantees elsewhere. (1) Worktree/venv provisioning: the entire env_transient machinery (verify.py:419-463 _ENV_TRANSIENT_PATTERNS, the forced-serial recovery retry at 2720-2766, sweep sentinels at 3552/3580) exists because task worktrees share one .venv that a concurrent `uv sync` from another orchestrator process can mutate mid-pytest (task 2048, grounded in task 2045). The missing upstream guarantee is venv isolation or an install lock; verify compensates with output-regex forensics that have already needed two anchoring fixes (32329ac44b, and the inverse-misattribution lookaheads). (2) git_ops: both probe functions retry `git worktree add` 3x with backoff (verify.py:3357-3368, 3521-3534) to absorb git's serialized worktree-metadata lock contention, and both carry the DD5 'never broad prune' invariant only as comments — the same broad-prune hazard that caused the warm-lane orphaned-registration incident (memory 2026-07-04) in git_ops territory. (3) workflow: b3_gate hard-aborts every merge-verify failure with 'no proposal to gate' because dry_run_proposals are produced only by workflow._spawn_dry_run_unblock at agent-block time (workflow.py:7769/7803/8228); the merge queue's block path never files one, so verify's cheapest failure class (trivial type/lint red) is structurally excluded from autonomous unblock and always lands on a human (matches operator memory feedback_b3_gate_aborts_on_merge_verify_no_proposal).

findings.title: Verify commands are opaque shell strings mutated by textual surgery — replace with a structured VerifyCmd rendered at spawn time
findings.problem: A verify command is a raw shell string from config, and every scoping/adaptation step is a find/replace hack on that string: _scope_command truncates at the first tool keyword and re-extracts dash-tokens (verify.py:85-115, explicitly 'naive dash-token extraction' per _build_fallback_config's docstring at 1559-1566), _strip_directory_flag does 4 replace() variants (204-219), _strip_leading_cd regex-strips one 'cd X &&' (222-243), _reproject_bare_uv_run rewrites 'uv run <tool>' into 'uv run --project shared <tool>' (254+), _scope_cargo_workspace substitutes --workspace and loops a regex until stable to strip --exclude pairs (1246-1279), _force_serial_pytest rewrites the pytest span (666), and _maybe_govern_merge_cmd wraps everything in bash -c (2399-2452). Each helper exists because a previous helper's output was un-runnable in some layout: _scope_command's truncation strands a leading 'cd fused-memory &&' (fixed by _strip_leading_cd, 4bb128496f), stripping --directory then broke uv venv resolution for structural files (dcfbd5ff11 preserves it in one branch), rewriting --workspace left an invalid --exclude (fd4758fcff). The tool identity, working directory, venv project, targets, and flags are all implicit in one string, so no transformation can be verified for well-formedness.
findings.proposal: Introduce a structured command model in a new module verify_cmd.py: @dataclass VerifyCmd(tool: ToolKind[PYTEST|RUFF|PYRIGHT|CARGO_TEST|CARGO_CLIPPY|NPX|OPAQUE], uv_project: str|None, cwd_rel: str|None, base_flags: tuple[str,...], targets: tuple[str,...], env: Mapping, wrappers: tuple[Wrapper,...]). Parse each config command string ONCE at config load (shlex-based; anything unparseable becomes ToolKind.OPAQUE and is never scoped — today it is scoped anyway and breaks). Scoping becomes 'replace targets', reprojection becomes 'set uv_project', cd-stripping becomes 'clear cwd_rel', cargo scoping becomes 'targets=[-p crate...]' with --exclude dropped structurally, cpu-governance becomes a wrapper entry. Render to a shell string only inside _run_cmd. All six string-rewrite helpers die. A single render() function can assert invariants (e.g. cwd_rel=None when targets are worktree-root-relative) that today are only comment lore.

findings.problem: The which-tests-for-this-diff decision is duplicated: scope_module_config (verify.py:1437-1545) and _build_fallback_config (1548-1691) each independently compute has_conftest, collectable_tests, and has_test_data and then take DIFFERENT fallback actions (module path: fall back to mc.test_command; fallback path: parent-dir targeting for conftest at 1638-1662, silent skip-with-warning for lone data modules at 1667-1684). Every file-classification bug had to be fixed in both places (task 1077 commits d7504d432d + cb7277926d; task 1852 commits 4fbed6c4fb + 7c9b316260). On top of that, run_scoped_verification duplicates the trivial-pass/pipeline-guard-override decision in its two branches (3140-3159 vs 3192-3211), and the overall scope decision is interleaved with execution so it is never inspectable except as log lines ('Verification mode: ...'). The structural-file (Protocol/TypedDict → unscoped pyright) check exists only in scope_module_config — the fallback path never widens pyright for structural files (a latent gap the 1852 pattern predicts will become a bug).
findings.proposal: New module verify_plan.py with a pure function derive_verify_plan(existing_files, module_configs, config, worktree_reader) -> VerifyPlan, where VerifyPlan is a list of PlannedRun(module_prefix, VerifyCmd, scope_kind: FULL_SUITE|FILE_SCOPED|SKIPPED|TRIVIAL, reason: str) plus plan-level flags (needs_pipeline_guard_check). File classification happens exactly once via a FileKind enum (CONFTEST, COLLECTABLE_TEST, TEST_DATA, STRUCTURAL, SOURCE, INERT) so predicates like _is_test_file/_is_collectable_test_file can't be recombined inconsistently. run_scoped_verification shrinks to derive-plan → execute-plan → aggregate. The plan is serializable, so it can be logged, unit-tested against the exact historical layouts (root conftest, data module, structural file), and attached to VerifyResult for post-hoc triage — closing the 'why did verify run/skip X' class permanently. The has_conftest-forces-full-suite convention (now CLAUDE.md operator lore) becomes an assertable property of the plan.

findings.title: Failure classifier is tool-blind: one regex ladder over all tools' merged output — dispatch on tool identity instead
findings.problem: _classify_failure (verify.py:522-566) and _extract_cause_hint (359-416) run the SAME pattern ladder over any check's output. _summarize_checks (703-749) calls them per-check but discards the one thing it knows — which command (and therefore which tool) produced the text. So every pattern must be safe against every tool's output universe: cargo prefixes must not swallow rustc diagnostics (the 3x re-grounding tasks 1103/1109/1116 — the allowlist comment block at 470-504 is a museum of dropped tokens), pytest progress lines pollute the fallback hint (405-413), infra tests that PRINT pytest-like markers polluted clock-stop matching (89256fc8e2), and the env_transient pip pattern needed a lookahead so 'pipeline'/'pipx' don't false-positive (32329ac44b, 442-457). This is the defining property behind BOTH mined classifier themes: patterns are written against assumed output shapes because no single tool's grammar bounds them.
findings.proposal: Make classification tool-dispatched: classify_failure(tool: ToolKind, rc: int, output: str, timed_out: bool) with per-tool classifier tables — cargo patterns only ever see cargo/clippy output, pytest patterns (incl. rc=5 semantics, INTERNALERROR, env_transient xdist-absence) only see pytest output, and the generic ladder survives only for ToolKind.OPAQUE. Where a tool offers structured output, prefer it over regex: pyright --outputjson, ruff --output-format json, cargo --message-format json (parse in the classifier, not the command — keep human logs). This removes the need to 'ground' each token against the union of all tools: a cargo allowlist token can no longer swallow a pytest or rustc line by construction. The env_transient patterns stop needing inverse-misattribution lookaheads because they run only under ToolKind.PYTEST. Depends naturally on the VerifyCmd model (finding 1) which carries tool identity to the call site — but can be shipped independently by keyword-sniffing the cmd string once, centrally.

findings.title: Category taxonomy is bare strings synced across 5+ registries and 3 consumer modules — replace with a FailureCategory enum + one policy table
findings.problem: VerifyResult.category is a free string whose per-category policy is scattered: _ARCHIVE_DENY_LIST (verify.py:577), _CATEGORY_PRIORITY ordering (584), PREEXISTING_BREAK_SKIP_CATEGORIES (606), the endswith('_error') archival convention in _should_archive_category (640-657), inline infra-sentinel sets {'pytest_internalerror','env_transient'} duplicated at run_main_tip_sweep:3552 and 3580, the env-recovery gate `category == 'env_transient'` at 2720, sentinel categories minted in a different module (verify_runner.py:109-115 UNSCOPED_TYPECHECK_*), and raw string comparisons in merge_queue.py:721/924 and workflow.py:4894/4939. Adding one category (env_transient, task 2048) required a dedicated commit literally titled 'wire env_transient into non-misattribution collections' (40012ffba3) touching every registry — and nothing detects a registry that was missed; a forgotten entry silently gets default behavior (unknown → lowest priority, not archived, probed on main).
findings.proposal: Define class FailureCategory(StrEnum) in a small verify_categories.py with a single declarative policy table: CATEGORY_POLICY: dict[FailureCategory, CategoryPolicy(severity_rank:int, archive:bool, preexisting_probe:bool, is_infra_transient:bool, retry_kind: NONE|TIMEOUT|ENV_SERIAL)]. Derive _CATEGORY_PRIORITY, _ARCHIVE_DENY_LIST, PREEXISTING_BREAK_SKIP_CATEGORIES, and the sweep's infra-sentinel set from the table; delete the endswith('_error') heuristic. A module-import-time assert enforces every enum member has a policy row (exhaustiveness). VerifyResult.category stays str on the wire (StrEnum keeps JSON codec byte-identical for verify_runner's Invariant 1) but all in-process branching goes through the enum. New categories then require exactly one row, and the retry behavior (currently three different ad-hoc retry mechanisms keyed on category/timeout flags) becomes visible in one place.

findings.title: B3 gate consumes a schemaless dict via string-prefix matching, and its required input artifact is never produced on the merge-verify path
findings.problem: Two coupled defects. (a) Contract: b3_gate reads metadata.dry_run_proposals[-1] straight out of tasks.db JSON (b3_gate.py:398-435) — a dict with no schema, where 'is this a failure entry' is inferred from the PRESENCE of a 'status' key (359-360) and the highest-blast-radius class is detected by block_reason.startswith(POST_MERGE_RED_MAIN_REASON_PREFIX) (341-352), a human-readable string re-declared from merge_queue and kept in sync only by a coherence test (b3_gate.py:42-51). Any producer rewording the block reason silently disables the hard-abort. (b) Coverage gap: proposals are written ONLY by workflow._spawn_dry_run_unblock at agent-block time (workflow.py:7769/7803/8228); merge_queue's block path writes block_reason but never a proposal, so check_proposal returns ABORT 'no proposal to gate' (b3_gate.py:312-319) for the ENTIRE merge-verify failure class — including the trivial scoped-lint/type reds that are B3's cheapest wins. Result: every merge-verify failure escalates to a human even when the fix is one import line (operator memory confirms this is a standing AFK pain point).
findings.proposal: Define a typed BlockRecord (dataclass in a new unblock_types.py: block_class: BlockClass enum {AGENT_FAILURE, REVIEW_ISSUES, MERGE_VERIFY_RED, POST_MERGE_RED_MAIN, ...}, risk_label, head_sha, main_sha, files_referenced, investigated_at) with to_dict/from_dict validation; workflow AND merge_queue construct it (merge_queue sets block_class explicitly instead of encoding it in prose), b3_gate branches on block_class — the re-declared prefix constant and the 'status'-key sniff die. Then close the coverage gap: merge_queue's block path spawns the same dry-run investigation (it already has worktree, failing VerifyResult, and scoped diff; the investigator's input is strictly richer than the agent-block case), with POST_MERGE_RED_MAIN remaining hard-abort by enum. This converts the biggest always-human escalation class into B3-gateable work while making the gate's precedence ladder type-checked rather than string-sniffed.

findings.title: Ephemeral probe-worktree lifecycle copy-pasted with a comment-only 'no broad prune' invariant — extract git_ops.ephemeral_worktree()
findings.problem: verify_failure_is_preexisting_on_main (verify.py:3315-3428) and run_main_tip_sweep (3496-3634) are structural clones: build path under git_ops.worktree_base with a magic prefix ('_mainprobe-'/'_mainsweep-'), 3-retry `git worktree add --detach` with linear backoff for git lock contention, and a finally block doing scoped `git worktree remove --force` + rmtree — with the safety invariant 'INTENTIONALLY NO git worktree prune (DD5)' stated three times as comments (3288, 3410, 3623) and enforced nowhere. Worse, the prefixes' protection from the disk-pressure reaper depends on prune_stale_merge_worktrees matching only '_merge-*' — a coincidence-of-globs contract spread across modules, exactly the shape that produced the warm-lane orphaned-registration incident where a broad `git worktree prune` from another subsystem wiped live registrations (July 2026 incident; fix task 2099 is a prune-guard). A third sibling (the _merge-* creation path in git_ops/merge_queue) implements the same lifecycle a third way.
findings.proposal: Add an async context manager to git_ops: ephemeral_worktree(kind: WorktreeKind, sha) -> Path, owning naming (prefix registry per kind), the retry-on-lock-contention loop, and guaranteed scoped cleanup. Maintain a module-level PROTECTED_PREFIXES registry derived from WorktreeKind so prune/reap routines (prune_stale_merge_worktrees, orphan reaper) consult it instead of hardcoded globs — turning the comment invariant into code. Enforce DD5 mechanically: a repo test (or the existing silent-fallthrough-gate style check) asserting no source file outside git_ops invokes `git worktree prune`. Both verify probes shrink to ~15 lines each; the retry policy stops drifting between copies (today one caller could get a fix the other misses, as happened with the archive-prune throttle history).
findings.bug_history_link: 87ba2e7509 (probe worktree moved under worktree_base — fixed in one copy first), f0289c4e2c (single SHA resolve hardening for sweep only); cross-system: warm-lane `git worktree prune` registration-wipe incident 2026-07-04 (df tasks 2097-2100, 2099=prune-guard) shows the comment-only prune invariant fails in practice

findings.title: run_verification's check state is nine parallel scalars with a hand-recomputed timeout-consistency formula — introduce a CheckRun dataclass
findings.problem: Each of the three checks is tracked as five parallel locals (test_rc/test_out/test_timed_out/test_started_at/test_duration ×3, verify.py:2631-2665), and the derived invariant 'timed_out flag must be consistent with per-check rc/timeout state' is a 6-clause boolean formula written out twice — in the retry loop (2672-2678) and again in the env-recovery branch (2747-2753). The inline comment at 2735-2744 documents the exact bug this duplication already produced: a recovery run hitting the wall-clock left a stale timed_out=False while category flipped to infra_timeout, wrongly marking the worktree warm and hiding the timeout from merge_queue/workflow callers. The same data is then re-materialized as ad-hoc dicts in `runs` (2769-2797) whose keys are a second implicit schema consumed by _persist_attempt_logs/_build_summary_payload/_verify_duration_secs.
findings.proposal: dataclass CheckRun(label, cmd, rc, output, timed_out, started_at, duration_secs) with classmethod skipped(), plus a small VerifyAttempt(checks: list[CheckRun]) exposing derived properties passed, any_timed_out, pure_timeout_failure — computed in exactly one place so first-pass and env-recovery cannot disagree. run_verification's loop carries one VerifyAttempt instead of 15 locals; `runs` becomes [c.to_dict() for c in attempt.checks], deleting the parallel dict schema. The 'pre-loop initialisation satisfies static analysis' scaffolding (2626-2636) and both formula copies die. This is a small, mechanical refactor that removes a documented drift-prone invariant.

clusters.architecture_notes: The task layer is a four-deck stack: server/tools.py (4k lines) is the MCP surface that normalizes project_root, runs a first copy of validation guards, and delegates to TaskInterceptor; middleware/task_interceptor.py (4.1k) is the policy layer — two-phase submit (ticket store + per-project asyncio worker queue), the curator dedup pipeline, path-scope guards, and a sequential gauntlet of status-transition gates (same-status, bulk-reset circuit breaker, terminal-exit, done-provenance, phantom-done, pre-done hook) in _apply_status_transition, all under per-project asyncio locks (_write_lock, _curator_lock); middleware/task_curator.py (2.6k) does LLM+embedding dedup with several in-memory caches; backends/sqlite_task_backend.py is per-project tasks.db with its own per-project_root lock/txn domain and a three-mode metadata merge (_resolve_metadata_mode/_merge_metadata). Key state: tasks.status is a free TEXT column with no legal-value enforcement, and tasks.metadata is a schemaless JSON blob carrying ~15 load-bearing keys (task_kind, before_done, always_escalates, external_deps, done_provenance, complexity, force_full_path, reblock_guard, dry_run_proposals, memory_hints, files, reopen stamps, routing_override_reason, escalation idempotency keys) consumed by the orchestrator in a separate process via .get() chains. Dependencies live in two representations: an integer table (verified at write) and metadata.external_deps strings (unverified, resolved at dispatch by the foreign scheduler). server/main.py wires everything, including a post-hoc circular reference (targeted.task_interceptor = task_interceptor, main.py:736-737) added to fix the reconciler's write-lock bypass (task 1136) — the direct-backend fallback still exists in targeted.py:666. tools.py additionally owns two scheduler-domain SQLite stores (scheduler_overrides.db, park_eviction_requests.db) that duplicate orchestrator modules line-for-line. The dominant seams are: (1) the metadata blob as an unversioned cross-process contract, (2) validation duplicated at every deck instead of privileged at one, and (3) a curator pipeline whose every failure branch degrades to CREATE.
clusters.cross_system_notes: Three concrete cross-subsystem patching flows. (1) fused-memory→orchestrator: server/tools.py:74-355 + 3437-3874 re-implements the orchestrator's scheduler_overrides.db and park_eviction_requests.db stores (DDL, pin_order allocation, BEGIN IMMEDIATE contract) because the MCP server must write files owned by the orchestrator's scheduler — kept in sync by 17 'Mirrors orchestrator/src/orchestrator/overrides.py:<line>' comments. (2) orchestrator→fused-memory schema drift: commit 9493fa073d — DeterministicRunner (orchestrator, task 1902) started writing done_provenance.kind='deterministic-deploy-scheduled'; fused-memory's _VALID_PROVENANCE_KINDS allowlist was never updated, so every own-unit self-restart deploy was rejected and landed silently blocked (tasks 1976/1982); the fix was another allowlist patch, not a shared schema. (3) Status vocabulary: task_interceptor.py:115-126 duplicates orchestrator.task_status.TERMINAL_STATUSES with an explicit 'duplication is cheaper than cross-package coupling' rationale, while orchestrator/task_status.py:16-21 carries a 'DRIFT RISK' warning and a CI test that imports the fused-memory set — i.e. the coupling exists anyway, just enforced in tests instead of code. Additionally, the interceptor's bulk-reset circuit breaker (task_interceptor.py:648-696) exists to defend against orchestrator/reconciler-side bulk status reversals (the 2026-04 reify incident), and reconciliation/targeted.py:653-670 retains a direct-backend fallback that bypasses the interceptor write lock (task 1136's fix was post-hoc wiring in main.py:736-737, not removal of the second path).

findings.title: Task metadata is an unversioned cross-process contract parsed by 8+ divergent best-effort parsers
findings.problem: metadata carries ~15 load-bearing keys consumed by the orchestrator (a different process) with no shared schema, no version, and no single parser. The subsystem contains at least 8 independent parse helpers with divergent failure semantics: task_interceptor.py:977-995 (_parse_metadata, unparseable→{}), 1428-1440 (_extract_metadata_dict, unparseable→None), 3860-3869 (inline parse in _merged_audit_metadata), deterministic_task_guard.py:48-60 (→{}), lock_charter_guard.py:179-181, tools.py:2354-2362 (→None, skip guard), sqlite_task_backend.py:280-294 (_row_to_task, warn-once + coerce {}), 1354-1431 (_merge_metadata, corrupt-existing→raise, corrupt-incoming→last-write-wins). Field vocabularies drift silently: producer and consumer each declare the schema in their own constants. sqlite_task_backend.py:1320-1351 (_normalize_legacy_memory_hints_value) exists solely to repair a shape drift that already shipped. The scheduler reads (task.get('metadata') or {}).get('external_deps') (scheduler.py:1996-1998) trusting a shape nothing enforces.
findings.proposal: Create shared/src/shared/task_metadata.py: a versioned pydantic model (TaskMetadata v1) with typed sub-models (BeforeDone, DoneProvenance, MemoryHints, ExternalDep) and a single parse_metadata() with one documented failure policy. shared/ is already imported by both sides (shared.usage_gate, shared.async_sqlite_base), so no new coupling. Enforce at the single write boundary — SqliteTaskBackend.add_task/update_task validate incoming blobs against the model (unknown keys pass through a reserved 'x_' namespace or warn) — and delete the 8 ad-hoc parsers in favor of the shared one. The orchestrator imports the same model for reads. Would have prevented: the deterministic-deploy-scheduled drift, the memory_hints legacy-shape class, and the external_deps shape assumptions.

Also _normalize_legacy_memory_hints_value repairing shipped shape drift; external-dep gate bugs 1854/1855/1799 (CLAUDE.md); before_done.cwd ignored by the runner (task 2105) — cwd/args/env are never validated because no schema names them.

findings.title: Curator dedup pipeline fails open to CREATE on every failure branch, forcing endless dedup layering
findings.problem: Every defensive branch in _process_add_tickets_batch_prepared degrades to 'create': idempotency-check failure → create (task_interceptor.py:2797-2800), curator exception → decisions=[None]*N → create (2926-2936), batch_target_index out of range → create (2867-2882), sibling failed → create (3001-3013), dependency cycle → create (3082-3097), worker cancelled mid-add_task → caller retry may duplicate (documented at 1553-1563). Since 'create' is the failure default, every new failure mode manifests as duplicate tasks — hence six stacked in-memory dedup layers, each with a DIFFERENT key: _intra_batch_key hashes title+description (task_curator.py:637-660) while _normalize_key hashes title+files (663-680), plus the R4 escalation-idempotency lookup, the LLM decision, the TTL'd _recent_creates cache (lost on restart), and the blocklist. The dispatch loop also maintains correlated parallel arrays across two index spaces ('non_none-space' vs 'ticket_data-space' remapping, 2843-2884) — the structure that produced the pass-1/pass-2 blank-title mismatch. No layer is durable: nothing at the store level makes duplicate creation impossible.
findings.proposal: Make uniqueness durable at the store: add a nullable candidate_key column to the tasks table (single normalization function, one key definition owned by task_curator.normalize_title + files) with a partial UNIQUE index over non-cancelled rows; add_task computes it, and a constraint violation resolves the ticket 'combined' with the existing id. This one root fix subsumes _recent_creates, _pre_llm_exact_match, and the intra-batch pre-pass (they become optimizations, not correctness layers) and survives restarts, which the in-memory caches do not. Separately, replace the parallel arrays (decisions[i], curator_degrade_reasons[i], resolved_task_ids[i], non_none_to_ticket_data) with a single per-ticket record dataclass so index-space remapping dies.

findings.title: update_task write-authority enforced by three drifting guard copies instead of one privileged seam
findings.problem: The invariant 'set_task_status is the only writer of status and done_provenance' is enforced by re-implementation at every deck: tools.py:2314-2373 (_reject_status_in_update_task, _reject_done_provenance_in_metadata), task_interceptor.py:3872-3934 (same two, labelled 'defence-in-depth alongside server/tools.py'), and a backend floor (sqlite_task_backend.py:804-810, status only). The copies already disagree on error shape — tools.py's done_provenance guard returns {'error':…,'error_type':'ValidationError'} while the interceptor's returns {'success':False,'error':'done_provenance_via_update_task'} — which forced interceptor_write_succeeded (task_interceptor.py:3958-3996) to enumerate every known rejection-dict shape. Root cause: writing done_provenance isn't a privileged capability — the sanctioned writer (_apply_status_transition, lines 719-724, 782-787) persists it through the SAME public tm.update_task it must guard, so 'who may write' can only be enforced by re-checking at every entry point, and the backend floor can never cover done_provenance.
findings.proposal: Make the backend the single enforcement point with a privileged internal API: SqliteTaskBackend.update_task unconditionally rejects status and metadata.done_provenance (extending the existing floor); add a non-protocol method stamp_audit_metadata(task_id, fields) that only TaskInterceptor holds a reference to, used for done_provenance/reopen_* persistence. Delete the tools.py and interceptor guard copies (tools.py keeps only the ticket-id shape check), and define the rejection dict shape once in task_backend_errors.py so interceptor_write_succeeded stops enumerating shapes.
findings.bug_history_link: 8daed1734a 'close update_task(status=) bypass + 4 defence-in-depth fixes' (2026-05-08 forensics: 9 unauthorized done writes in 36h); 92d9c7d28e 'backend floor rejects non-None status' — the third layer added because the first two could be bypassed by in-process callers; 3daade6fd8 done_provenance kind discriminator + role gate.

findings.title: Status vocabulary duplicated in four modules with zero store-level enforcement
findings.problem: tasks.status is 'TEXT NOT NULL' with no CHECK (sqlite_task_backend.py:62), and set_task_status writes any string verbatim (658-692). The legal vocabulary is declared four times: orchestrator/task_status.py:11-45 (TERMINAL/ACTIVE/WORKFLOW_PRESERVE, with an explicit 'DRIFT RISK' comment warning that a stale set silently strands tasks from dispatch), fused_memory/reconciliation/task_filter.py:217 (ACTIVE_TASK_STATUSES), task_interceptor.py:115-126 (TERMINAL_STATUSES, comment: 'Duplicated from orchestrator.task_status… duplication is cheaper than cross-package coupling' — contradicted by the CI guard test that already imports across packages, and by shared/ being an existing cross-consumed package). A typo'd or novel status ('in_progress' vs 'in-progress') persists silently, falls outside ACTIVE_TASK_STATUSES, and the task is never fetched or dispatched again — silent stranding, the worst failure shape this system has.
findings.proposal: One shared/src/shared/task_statuses.py exporting a StrEnum plus the derived frozensets (TERMINAL, ACTIVE, WORKFLOW_PRESERVE, STATUS_TRIGGERS); SqliteTaskBackend.set_task_status/add_task reject status not in the enum (loud TaskmasterError), optionally backed by a CHECK constraint at the next schema bump. Both packages import it; delete the three local copies and the cross-package equality test (it becomes tautological). Adding a status ('merge-deferred' took synchronized edits in 3 files + 2 regression tests per the task-1519 comments) becomes a one-line change.
findings.bug_history_link: task 1519 'merge-deferred' required coordinated edits in task_interceptor.py:120-126, orchestrator/task_status.py, and two lock-tests; 475b16dbce 'trust store over stale _status_cache for reinstated tasks'; mined theme 4x backend/protocol conformance drift (eb21502b68).

findings.title: Path-guard routes tasks by regex over prose, compensated by a four-stage patch stack plus a permanent 'temporary' shim
findings.problem: Project routing is decided by regex-scanning free prose (title/description/details) for path prefixes (path_scope_guard.py:34-63, hand-tuned boundary class excluding '/' and '.'), where mention ≠ ownership — so precision/recall is structurally unwinnable at the regex layer. The system compensated by stacking: lookbehind tuning (tasks 1095/1096/1100/1111/1118), a 454-line LLM adjudicator on guard HIT (path_scope_adjudicator.py, task 1822), a routing_override_reason escape hatch (task 1845), and a scope-violation escalator. Meanwhile dark_factory_path_guard.py declares itself a back-compat shim 'for one merge cycle' yet is still the import used by task_interceptor.py:34-38, keeping two guard mechanisms (registry-configured multi-project vs hard-coded dark-factory short-circuit, _path_guard_check task_interceptor.py:1057+) alive in parallel.
findings.proposal: Split the decision by signal quality: REJECT only on structured evidence — metadata.files prefixes matched exactly against ProjectPrefixRegistry (no regex, no prose) — and demote prose scanning to an advisory: attach a 'possible_scope_mismatch' warning to the created task / fire the escalator instead of rejecting, letting the existing adjudicator+curator handle the ambiguous middle asynchronously. This ends the FP/FN tuning treadmill because exact file-prefix matching has no recall/precision dial. Delete the dark_factory_path_guard shim by switching the interceptor's imports to path_scope_guard and folding the hard-coded prefix list into the registry default.
findings.bug_history_link: 6x mined theme: task 1088 (introduce guard), 1094 'prompt-only bypass', 1095 'false positives: tighten lookbehind', 1096/1100/1111/1118 successive polish; then 1822 (adjudicator) and 1845 (override hatch) as compensation layers; meta-fix task 2085 for the mis-routing class.

findings.title: Deterministic-task invariants enforced only at submit_task; update_task can violate them, and malformed metadata is silently discarded
findings.problem: The B10 invariants (task_kind enum, deterministic⇒before_done∨always_escalates, before_done only on deterministic, script exists+executable+timeout_secs) run once at tools.py submit_task (tools.py:2804-2810). update_task's guards reject only status/done_provenance/directory-locks (task_interceptor.py:3144-3155) — nothing stops update_task(metadata={'task_kind':'deterministic'}) on a normal task, injecting or mutating before_done (e.g. pointing script at a path that no longer exists), or flipping always_escalates, all of which the DeterministicRunner in the orchestrator will trust at dispatch. Separately, deterministic_task_guard._parse_metadata (48-60) maps an unparseable metadata string to {}, so validation passes vacuously AND inject_task_kind (236-238) then REPLACES the caller's entire metadata with {'task_kind':'normal'} — silent data loss with no warning (contrast _inject_routing_override, task_interceptor.py:1451-1467, which at least warns).
findings.proposal: Two enforcement moves: (1) extend the interceptor's update_task guard chain with _reject_kind_fields_in_update_metadata rejecting any metadata write that touches task_kind/before_done/always_escalates unless it passes deterministic_task_error() against the POST-merge blob (fetch-merge-validate under the existing write lock); (2) make submit_task fail loudly on unparseable metadata strings (ValidationError) instead of best-effort-{} — the interceptor already fails fast on non-serializable kwargs (task_interceptor.py:1625-1637), so this matches existing policy. Both collapse into the shared TaskMetadata schema (finding 1) if that lands first.
findings.bug_history_link: Partially speculative for the update_task bypass (no incident yet); the silent-discard is the same class as the routing-override data-loss note, and the before_done validate-at-submit-only gap is adjacent to task 2105 (before_done.cwd never validated, detached self-restart 127 failures) and the 1962 deferred-filer pattern that exists precisely because before_done is only checked at submit time.

clusters.hotspot: fm-recon (fused-memory LLM-driven reconciliation pipeline: harness.py, stages/task_knowledge_sync.py, flag_dedup.py, targeted.py, stages/memory_consolidator.py, prompts/stage1.py, prompts/stage2.py)
clusters.architecture_notes: The harness (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/harness.py) runs one asyncio loop per project; each cycle (run_full_cycle) resolves project_root from a {project_id -> project_root} registry (_known_project_root_for, harness.py:504), fetches a filtered task tree, then executes three stages, each of which is a full Claude CLI invocation with MCP tools gated only by per-stage disallow-lists (cli_stage_runner.py:64-66): Stage 1 MemoryConsolidator (memory writes, no task writes), Stage 2 TaskKnowledgeSync (unrestricted memory AND task writes including submit_task/set_task_status), Stage 3 IntegrityCheck (read-only). A judge scores each run and a remediation pass (harness.py:2409) can re-run stages against persistent Stage-3 findings; TargetedReconciler (targeted.py) handles per-status-transition reconciliation events. Durable state is split across three stores with very different guarantees: SQLite (journal, write journal, event buffer — transactional), the escalation queue (JSON files), and — critically — Mem0 itself, where the pipeline keeps its own control-plane records (stage1_flag_marker, stage1_flag_suppression, stage2_persistence_marker, flag_for_stage2 relay, fixc markers, stage1/stage2 cycle_summary pool entries) as vector-store memories. Because the stage agents are amnesiac LLMs, cross-cycle continuity is maintained entirely through these Mem0 marker records plus prompt-rendered payload sections, and the LLM's own writes are policed after the fact: stats_verifier overwrites LLM-self-reported counters from the write journal, and Stage 2's _apply_post_flight_guards (task_knowledge_sync.py:2730) re-parses the run's journal ops to reclassify illegal task writes it could not prevent. TaskKnowledgeSync.run() (task_knowledge_sync.py:2527-2728) is an accretion of ~10 sequential compensations: pool pre-trim, dup suppression, four post-flight guards, summary verify->repair->reconstruct chain, and four distinct marker GC sweeps, each added by a separate fix task. The git log shows 871 commits touching reconciliation/ since 2026-04-01 — this is the single hottest fix surface in fused-memory.
clusters.cross_system_notes: Three clear cross-subsystem compensation patterns. (1) Mem0/MemoryService dedup layer: the reconciliation prompts (prompts/stage1.py:121-180, prompts/stage2.py:237-295) instruct the LLM to prepend CSPRNG summary_nonce and construct deterministic retry_nonce lines purely to defeat the memory service's ~0.92-cosine silent dedup of recon's own per-cycle writes, and Python then read-back-verifies, metadata-repairs, and finally fabricates a reconstruction placeholder when the write was still swallowed (task_knowledge_sync.py:2629-2680). The missing upstream guarantee is a dedup-exempt system-write path in MemoryService. (2) middleware/task_interceptor: Stage 2's post-flight guards exist because the interceptor enforces its terminal-exit/bulk-reset/done-provenance gates generically but offers no per-agent write policy for recon agents — _classify_terminal_state_violations (task_knowledge_sync.py:283) states outright that 'skip the write entirely cannot be enforced post-hoc ... reclassifies the op instead'. (3) orchestrator TDD pipeline: recon files tasks with no executability contract, so operational/live-data work lands in the architect+TDD pipeline that cannot act on it (operator-confirmed recurring class, meta-fix task 2085; false-premise batch 2083/2092/2093), producing architect refusals and churn in the orchestrator subsystem.

findings.title: Recon control-plane state (markers, suppressions, counters, summaries) lives in Mem0, an eventually-consistent deduplicating vector store
findings.problem: At least six kinds of system records (stage1_flag_marker, stage1_flag_suppression, stage2_persistence_marker, flag_for_stage2, fixc markers, stage1/stage2 cycle_summary) are stored as Mem0 memories and used as a transactional dedup/lifecycle ledger. Mem0 offers no atomic replace, no read-after-write consistency, and silently drops similar writes, so flag_dedup.py's 241-line module docstring (flag_dedup.py:1-241) narrates seven stacked compensations: best-effort write-then-delete replacement (non-atomic, leaves transient duplicates), in-batch memoization for read-after-write lag (task-1978), post-write read-back confirmation with one retry (task-1400), a per-invocation confirmation circuit-breaker (task-1412), a limit=50 reclamation bound, and self-healing-on-next-cycle semantics. On the consumer side TaskKnowledgeSync.run() needs FOUR separate GC sweeps (_sweep_stale_fixc_markers task_knowledge_sync.py:1192, _sweep_stale_flag_markers:1246, _sweep_terminal_task_flag_markers:1424, _sweep_stale_persistence_markers:1624), each added by a separate incident-driven task, because there is no TTL or status predicate on the store itself.
findings.proposal: Introduce ReconLedgerStore: a SQLite table (the codebase already runs transactional SQLite for the journal, write journal, and event buffer) with schema (project_id, record_kind, task_id, flag_type, run_id, payload_json, created_at, expires_at, state) and PRIMARY KEY on the identity tuple. Marker replacement becomes a single UPSERT transaction (kills the write/confirm/delete dance, the circuit breaker, and the in-batch memo); all four GC sweeps collapse to one 'DELETE WHERE expires_at < now OR referenced-task-terminal' pass; suppression lookup becomes an indexed query instead of a project-wide semantic search. Mem0 keeps only a best-effort human-searchable mirror of narrative content. flag_dedup.py shrinks to signature computation + ledger calls; the marker sections of task_knowledge_sync.py move into the ledger module (real seam: single-writer marker lifecycle).
findings.bug_history_link: Tasks 1097/1120/1121/1122/1128/1134/1146 (marker GC/None-metadata/atomicity re-fixes), 1144/1145 (Stage 1 snapshot/marker atomicity, still open at snapshot), 1944/f5e60b43cd and 2103 and 2095 (three separate new sweeps), 2047/16ce25d4c6 (fp: marker enrichment), 1786/5c77b2dbc6 (unique_groups IndexError), 2026-07-05 solar_challenge_platform 16-record manual bulk GC incident cited at task_knowledge_sync.py:2698-2708.

findings.title: Recon's own per-cycle writes are routed through the LLM-facing dedup pipeline, spawning the nonce arms race and a verify/repair/reconstruct chain
findings.problem: Because MemoryService.add_memory silently dedups at ~0.92 cosine similarity, the stage prompts teach the LLM to prepend a Python-generated CSPRNG summary_nonce line and, on dedup-retry, to construct a deterministic retry_nonce (prompts/stage1.py:121-180, prompts/stage2.py:237-295; generate_summary_nonce cli_stage_runner.py:240-303). When the write is still swallowed, Python compensates post-hoc: _verify_stage2_summary_written (task_knowledge_sync.py:1825) confirms via count_memories_by_metadata, _repair_stage2_summary_stage_metadata (:1890) re-adds identity metadata, and _reconstruct_stage2_summary (:2040) fabricates a placeholder record (run() wiring at :2629-2680). This is a genuine arms race: a prior nonce fix reused an already-embedded token and re-triggered the same 0.92 dedup it aimed to defeat (commit 2777f2b227). The upstream defect is that the memory service has no dedup-exempt write path for machine-generated, per-run records.
findings.proposal: Add a dedup-exempt system-write path in MemoryService — add_memory(..., dedup_exempt=True) or a dedicated add_system_record operation — permitted only for recon-stage agent_ids and enforced server-side (the interceptor already discriminates by agent_id in the write journal). Then delete: all summary_nonce/retry_nonce prompt directives, generate_summary_nonce/build_summary_nonce_section, and the entire verify->repair->reconstruct chain (three functions plus their run() wiring and four stats keys). Cycle summaries get written once, deterministically, by Python after the stage completes (content from the StageReport), removing the LLM from the reliability path entirely.
findings.bug_history_link: Nonce-hardening series tasks 1590/1796/1821 and commit 2777f2b227 (Stage 1 retry_nonce realignment); tasks 1963 (stage-metadata repair, 5e7b501c33/0e4b036974) and 1964 (fully-absent reconstruction, cbd4f1fc68/1254e1da3a) exist solely because dedup swallowed recon's own summary writes; confirmed incidents run 6467daca and 2026-07-01 cited in task_knowledge_sync.py:2634-2660.

findings.title: project_id and project_root are interchangeable bare strs threaded through every signature, with mutable post-construction injection into stages
findings.problem: Both identifiers are plain str and travel side by side through dozens of signatures (e.g. targeted.py:378 '_on_task_done(self, task_id: str, project_id: str, project_root: str, ...)', :622, :1143), so swapping them type-checks clean and fails only at runtime — the mined 10x bug class. Task 1143's registry hard-bind (_known_project_root_for, harness.py:504-539) fixed the harness entry point but not the mechanism: BaseStage defaults self.project_root to '' (stages/base.py:61) and relies on the harness remembering to inject it after construction (harness.py:1832, 2523); downstream code then 'degrades to a no-op (0) when taskmaster or project_root is unset' (task_knowledge_sync.py:2706-2708) — a silent-skip failure mode for a forgotten injection. Every new call site re-creates the swap opportunity, which is why the fix chain (156, 186, 927, then 930/931/932/948/958/959/961/963) spanned weeks.
findings.proposal: Introduce a frozen dataclass ProjectScope(project_id: ProjectId, project_root: ProjectRoot) using typing.NewType for both fields, constructed in exactly one place — _known_project_root_for at cycle entry (which also asserts os.path.isabs) — and threaded as a single parameter through harness, stages, targeted.py, and the sweep/guard helpers. BaseStage takes scope as a required __init__ argument (delete the '' default and the post-construction attribute injection). Because pyright already gates every merge, any future project_id/project_root transposition at a new call site becomes a compile-time type error instead of a runtime cross-project contamination bug.
findings.bug_history_link: Tasks 156 ('targeted.py project_root fallback silently uses project_id as path'), 186 (task_knowledge_sync lines 46/99), 927 ('_fetch_filtered_task_tree receives project_id as fallback'), follow-ups 930/931/932/948/958/959/961/963, cancelled duplicate 880, and 1143 (registry hard-bind, the partial structural fix this completes).

findings.title: Stage 2 write invariants are enforced post-hoc by journal forensics instead of at the interceptor write boundary
findings.problem: The Stage 2 LLM holds unrestricted task-write tools (STAGE2_DISALLOWED blocks only built-ins, cli_stage_runner.py:65). Invariants like 'never update_task a terminal task', 'never write status to a task under a live workflow', and 'snapshot must be fresh at write time' are checked only AFTER the run by _apply_post_flight_guards (task_knowledge_sync.py:2730-2988), which re-fetches every touched task and reclassifies journal ops — _classify_terminal_state_violations (:283) admits 'the skip-the-write semantics cannot be enforced post-hoc (the LLM's write already landed), so this helper reclassifies the op instead'. Meanwhile the interceptor already enforces a server-side terminal FSM for set_task_status (terminal-exit gate task_interceptor.py:702, bulk-reset guard :685, done-provenance gate :744) but has no per-agent policy covering recon's update_task-on-terminal or live-workflow cases. The result: bad writes land, counters get corrected, and each newly discovered liveness signal (plan.lock, owner_pid, branch ancestry, deleted branch) became another incremental guard fix.
findings.proposal: Move enforcement to the single write boundary: a ReconWritePolicy consulted inside the interceptor's _apply_status_transition and update_task paths whenever agent_id starts with 'recon-stage-' — reject update_task when live status is in TERMINAL_STATUSES, reject status writes when services.live_workflow_detector.is_workflow_live_for_task is true, and require a payload-issued snapshot token whose staleness the server checks (replacing the post-hoc stall-guard freshness gate). Rejections return structured errors the LLM can read mid-run (like the existing DarkFactoryPathScopeViolation). _apply_post_flight_guards then shrinks from a ~650-line forensic suite to pure counter reconciliation, and the rejected-write class of stranded/terminal mutations becomes impossible rather than detected.
findings.bug_history_link: Task 1137 ('enforce terminal-state pre-check, stall-guard freshness gate' — the guard suite), task 1655/69dd6139d3 (Guard 5 live-workflow classifier), and the 9x stranded-in-progress hardening chain 886/911/912/913/916/1087/1092/1106/1114 where each new liveness edge case was patched into prompts+guards instead of the write path.

findings.title: LLM-authored counters are the primary stats channel, perpetually reconciled against journal-derived reality by three separate mechanisms
findings.problem: Stage agents self-report counts (memories_added, tasks_modified, flagged_count); reality is derived from the write journal. Three independent reconcilers exist: stats_verifier.py overwrites self-reported values via a hand-maintained _OP_TO_STAT map plus an alias map for names 'the LLM may emit' (stats_verifier.py:29-59 — the alias map is itself a patch for prompt drift); _check_flag_counter_completeness and _check_mem0_flag_counter_completeness (task_knowledge_sync.py:591, 644) audit flag counters separately; and the post-flight guards decrement tasks_modified when writes are reclassified (:2843-2847). Every counter not yet in the map is a latent drift bug, and the judge flags mismatches as run-quality problems, generating follow-up fix tasks.
findings.proposal: Invert the source of truth: report.stats is COMPUTED, not reported. Add one derivation function beside WriteJournal (derive_stage_stats(ops, stage_agent_id) -> dict) that produces every write-shaped counter from journal ops; StageReport.stats is populated exclusively from it, with the LLM's numbers preserved only under stats['_reported'] for the judge's divergence signal (the pattern stats_verifier already half-implements). Enforce with a stats-key allowlist in the report schema so a new counter cannot be introduced as an LLM-reported field. stats_verifier's alias map and both flag-counter completeness checkers die.
findings.bug_history_link: Tasks 1150 ('memories_written count' — the exact alias in _STAT_ALIASES), 1589/ee2dca83d1 (counter amendments), 5b820f3bcd (inc_stat prompt kwarg fix), and the open-at-snapshot Stage 1/2 correctness cluster item on counter completeness; root mechanism documented in stats_verifier.py:1-10 (Mem0 silent dedup makes agents over-report).

findings.title: Recon files tasks with no machine-checkable premise or executability contract — the self-model lives only in drifting prompt prose
findings.problem: Stage 2 can submit_task into any known project (prompts/stage2.py:31-66); the only gates are the curator ticket flow (dedup/combine — validates neither the finding's factual premise nor whether the work is executable by the TDD pipeline) and the path-scope guard (project routing only). The system's self-model — what markers mean, how fingerprint dedup anchors work, exact tool-call shapes — is hand-transcribed into prompt prose that provably drifts from code: stage2.py:103-125 narrates _derive_affected_ids and compute_content_fingerprint internals to coax dedup-compatible behavior; commit a2327a65e1 fixed a system/user-prompt disagreement on count_memories_by_metadata arg shape; the false-premise cleanup batch 2083/2092/2093 was filed on a wrong model of stage1_flag_marker/run_id behavior that nothing could check. Filed tasks also carry no execution-class field, so operational live-data work is dispatched to the TDD architect pipeline that must refuse it.
findings.proposal: Two enforcement points. (a) Single-source the self-model: a recon_self_model.py module that exports the mechanism constants and invariants (marker kinds and their lifecycle, fingerprint identity fields, dedup thresholds, exact MCP call signatures) and RENDERS the prompt sections describing them — prompts import the rendered text instead of hand-duplicating it, so prompt/code drift becomes structurally impossible, and the same module exposes assertable predicates (e.g. 'run_id is fresh-per-run', 'markers are deleted only by sweeps X/Y') that a premise-lint can run against recon-authored task descriptions before filing. (b) Require metadata.execution_class in {code_tdd, operational, decision} on every recon-filed submit_task, validated at the curator (reject absent/unknown), with 'operational' routed to the recon escalation queue (port 8103 watcher) instead of the orchestrator's TDD dispatch — encoding the actionability contract the operator memory shows is missing.
findings.bug_history_link: False-premise batch 2083/2092/2093 (filed on a wrong stage1_flag_marker model, unactionable-on-TDD, human abandon-closed); task 2085 (meta-fix for operational live-data tasks mis-routed to TDD, recurring class); commit a2327a65e1 (prompt/system drift on call shape); operator memory 'recon files tasks that are unactionable on the TDD pipeline'.

clusters.hotspot: shared-infra: shared/src/shared/usage_gate.py (1376 lines, 68% fix ratio) + shared/src/shared/cli_invoke.py (1586 lines), plus consumers (orchestrator steward/harness/workflow, fused-memory curator/recon)
clusters.architecture_notes: The stack is layered: _run_subprocess (cli_invoke.py:1328) owns process supervision — spawn with start_new_session, a two-regime liveness watchdog that reads the on-disk JSONL transcript to detect pre-first-turn wedges, SIGTERM/SIGKILL process-group teardown; _invoke_claude (cli_invoke.py:1004) assembles argv/env (temp-file prompts, StructuredOutput denylist expansion, vLLM bridge, sandbox wrap); _parse_claude_output (cli_invoke.py:1141) turns the CLI JSON envelope into AgentResult (success/subtype/is_error/schema_salvaged/api_error_status). Above that, invoke_with_cap_retry (cli_invoke.py:660-1001) is a ~340-line policy loop mixing crash-recovery resume protocol, 401/403 auth failover, zero-output wedge guard, cap-pattern detection, a zero-cost heuristic cap detector, resume-to-fresh fallback, exponential cooldown, a 14-day sanity bound, and cost-store persistence. UsageGate (usage_gate.py:204) is a per-process, in-memory asyncio account pool: AccountState carries six scattered flags (capped/near_cap/probing/probe_in_flight/auth_failed + timestamps + two background asyncio.Task handles); before_invoke selects the first account passing 'not capped/probe_in_flight/auth_failed'; background resume-probe and auth-reprobe loops fire real haiku invocations through a single shared TaskConfigDir('usage-gate-probe') under /tmp; SIGHUP wholesale-resets all flags and probes all accounts in parallel. InvokeSlot (usage_gate.py:147) is a retrofitted context manager guaranteeing probe-slot release, but callers still reach into gate privates (_handle_auth_failure, _handle_cap_detected at cli_invoke.py:806/932) and must manually slot.settle(). orchestrator/src/orchestrator/usage_gate.py is NOT a fork — it is a 10-line pure re-export shim of shared.usage_gate (no drift risk). The steward (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/steward.py:536-607) bypasses invoke_with_cap_retry with its own hand-rolled, already-divergent cap-retry loop. There is no cross-process coordination: check_at_startup is a no-op and cap state is rediscovered independently by each of the ~6 fleet orchestrator processes plus fused-memory's curator/reconciliation runners sharing the same 6-account pool.
clusters.cross_system_notes: Two directions. (1) Compensation FOR the upstream Claude CLI (external subsystem): the two-regime transcript-reading watchdog in _run_subprocess (cli_invoke.py:1377-1491), zero-output wedge classification via on-disk JSONL transcripts (1778-series commits), the StructuredOutput '*'-denylist expansion for the CLI 2.1.168 regression (cli_invoke.py:172-215, 1066-1070), NON_CAP_CLI_ERROR_MARKERS for --session-id collisions, and the entire cap-prose scraping stack all exist because the CLI gives no structured liveness/rate-limit/tool-policy contract — this is the largest single source of fix commits in the hotspot. (2) Duplicated defence ACROSS internal subsystems: the wedge guard in invoke_with_cap_retry (cli_invoke.py:821-853) explicitly cites fused-memory/reconciliation/agent_loop.py:368's 'clear stale session id' defence as its analogue — the same stale-session invariant ('never re-resume a session that produced zero turns') is enforced independently in shared and in fused-memory's reconciliation loop, and a third variant lives in the c51ff98aa5 'wedge guard to clear stale resume session' commit; it belongs once in shared, consumed by both. Additionally, the orchestrator harness encodes a shutdown-ordering workaround for gate internals (harness.py:1618-1636: cancel workflows BEFORE usage_gate.shutdown() lest _handle_cap_detected respawn probe tasks after drain) — a lifecycle invariant that should be enforced inside UsageGate.shutdown (refuse/absorb new probe tasks once shutting down) rather than by caller ordering.

findings.title: AccountState is a 6-flag bag encoding an unenforced 6-state machine; every transition site must manually clear the other flags
findings.problem: An account is really in exactly one phase — AVAILABLE, PROBING(open slot), PROBE_IN_FLIGHT, CAPPED, AUTH_FAILED (near_cap is an annotation) — but this is stored as independent booleans (usage_gate.py:113-136). Every transition is an ad-hoc multi-flag mutation that must remember to clear the others: _handle_cap_detected clears near_cap/probing/probe_in_flight (446-449), _handle_auth_failure clears probe flags (515-518), SIGHUP resets 9 fields (692-700), _refresh_capped_accounts sets probing (825-827), the probe-loop success branch sets 5 fields (886-895), and the auth_failed→capped demotion in _run_probe needs ~40 lines of ordering commentary and explicit pre-clearing so 'capped + auth_failed' doesn't coexist (997-1027). The global _open event is recomputed at 6 different sites (303, 335, 465, 535, 601, 834, 897, 1177, 1211), any of which can be missed. Background task lifecycle (resume_task/auth_reprobe_task) is likewise managed per-site.
findings.proposal: Introduce AccountPhase(StrEnum) with a legal-transition table and make a single `UsageGate._transition(acct, new_phase, *, resets_at=None, reason='')` the ONLY writer of phase state. The method: (1) asserts the transition is legal (raises/logs loudly on illegal ones like AUTH_FAILED→PROBE_IN_FLIGHT), (2) owns side effects per target phase — cancel/start resume/reprobe tasks, fire the cost event, stamp pause_started_at, (3) recomputes the global _open event from `any(a.phase is AVAILABLE/PROBING)` in one place. near_cap stays a separate annotation cleared by the transition function. All handlers (_handle_cap_detected, _handle_auth_failure, _on_sighup_async, _refresh_capped_accounts, probe loops, confirm_account_ok, release_probe_slot) shrink to `self._transition(...)` calls.

findings.title: Invocation-outcome classification is computed in five places with different rules; cli_invoke reaches into UsageGate privates to apply its verdicts
findings.problem: The decision 'what did this CLI invocation mean?' is duplicated with divergent rules: (1) UsageGate.detect_cap_hit — prefix + CAP_CONFIRM_KEYWORDS guard (usage_gate.py:366-428); (2) _run_probe — prefix-only, a deliberate asymmetry defended by a 20-line do-not-fix comment (usage_gate.py:972-1028); (3) invoke_with_cap_retry — its own 401/403 auth routing (cli_invoke.py:805), zero-output wedge guard (842), zero-cost heuristic cap detector plus NON_CAP_CLI_ERROR_MARKERS exclusion table (905-964, 120-132); (4) _parse_claude_output — is_error/subtype/salvage semantics (1141-1248); (5) classify_agent_failure — a parallel AgentFailureKind taxonomy for the steward (453-538). Because the InvokeSlot abstraction only auto-settles on detect_cap_hit/confirm, the retry loop must call gate privates usage_gate._handle_auth_failure (cli_invoke.py:806) and usage_gate._handle_cap_detected (cli_invoke.py:932) and remember slot.settle() — exactly the seam where the 4x probe-slot-leak fixes landed. Each new CLI wording or error shape must be patched into 2-3 of these tables independently.
findings.proposal: Create shared/src/shared/invocation_outcome.py with a sum type `InvocationOutcome = OK | CapHit(resets_at, reason) | NearCap(reason) | AuthFailed(status) | CliLocalError(marker) | ZeroOutputWedge | Failure(kind)` and one classifier `classify_invocation(result: AgentResult, *, strict_confirm: bool, backend: str) -> InvocationOutcome` holding ALL string tables (CAP_HIT_PREFIXES, CAP_CONFIRM_KEYWORDS, NON_CAP_CLI_ERROR_MARKERS, CODEX/GEMINI patterns) adjacent, with the probe's prefix-only policy expressed as strict_confirm=False instead of a separate loop. Replace the private reach-ins with one public `InvokeSlot.report(outcome)` that performs the matching gate transition AND settles the slot atomically — making 'slot settled iff gate informed' an enforced invariant rather than caller discipline. classify_agent_failure becomes a projection of InvocationOutcome.

findings.title: Steward hand-rolls a second cap-retry loop that has already drifted from invoke_with_cap_retry
findings.problem: steward._invoke_steward (steward.py:536-607) reimplements the invoke_slot/detect_cap_hit/resume-on-next-account loop and has diverged from the canonical invoke_with_cap_retry on every policy axis: fixed 5s cooldown vs exponential backoff; bounded _MAX_CAP_RETRIES then RuntimeError vs 14-day patient wait + AllAccountsCappedException; no 401/403 auth-failure routing; no zero-output wedge guard (a wedged steward session gets re-resumed forever); no zero-cost heuristic cap detection; no NON_CAP_CLI_ERROR_MARKERS exclusion. The fix history shows the same defect class being patched independently in both copies — the definition of a defect-generating structure.
findings.proposal: Delete the steward loop and route it through invoke_with_cap_retry, extending the shared function with the two hooks the steward actually needs: (a) an optional `rebuild_prompt: Callable[[bool session_lost], Awaitable[str]]` invoked on cap-retry when the session cannot be resumed (steward rebuilds its initial prompt with fresh pending escalations), and (b) an optional `max_cap_retries: int | None` bound for callers that must not wait 14 days. Steward keeps only session-id bookkeeping. Same treatment for any future caller tempted to hand-roll (grep gate.invoke_slot outside cli_invoke: steward is the only remaining one).

findings.title: Account identity re-derived by a predicate that disagrees with the selection predicate — cost/log attribution can name the wrong account
findings.problem: before_invoke selects an account with the predicate `not (capped or probe_in_flight or auth_failed)` (usage_gate.py:296) but returns only the bare token. InvokeSlot.__init__ then re-derives the name via gate.active_account_name (usage_gate.py:171), whose predicate omits probe_in_flight (1137-1139). Concrete failure: account[0] is PROBE_IN_FLIGHT (claimed by another task), a second caller is handed account[1]'s token, yet its slot.account_name — used for cost_store.save_invocation and failover logs at cli_invoke.py:782/863/979-998 — reports account[0]. The same identity-by-token-string pattern (_find_account_by_token, _resolve_account fallback) already produced misattribution bugs. All attribution downstream (dashboard per-account cost, cap_hit events) inherits the error.
findings.proposal: Make before_invoke return the selected AccountState (or an immutable AccountLease dataclass with name+token+generation) instead of a raw token; InvokeSlot carries the lease, and every gate mutation path takes the lease rather than doing token-equality resolution (_resolve_account/_find_account_by_token become fallbacks for token-only external callers only). Delete the active_account_name re-derivation in the invoke path. This makes 'the account you report on is the account you invoked with' a type-level invariant.
findings.bug_history_link: 18c6a6c393 '_resolve_account: return None for explicit unknown tokens (no fallback)' fixed the same misattribution class; 4359d3f35c 'correct cap-status logic' and 0bd57513d9 'capture probe_count before reset in cost-event label' are attribution-drift siblings. The probe_in_flight name-skew itself is unfixed today (speculative as a shipped incident, confirmed in code).

findings.title: Cap/reset signal scraped from human-facing CLI prose with silent fallbacks — the structural driver of the string-matching arms race
findings.problem: The upstream Claude CLI provides no machine-readable rate-limit status in its JSON envelope, so this layer compensates by scraping wording: CAP_HIT_PREFIXES/CAP_CONFIRM_KEYWORDS (usage_gate.py:48-78) chase verbatim marketing copy ('You're now using extra…'); _parse_resets_at (usage_gate.py:1266-1363) regex-parses 'resets Mar 30, 6pm (Europe/London)' and SILENTLY falls back to now+1h on any parse failure — that fabricated time then drives probe scheduling, soonest_resets_at, and dashboard ETAs; the zero-cost heuristic (cli_invoke.py:910) exists because pattern matching is known-incomplete, and NON_CAP_CLI_ERROR_MARKERS exists because the heuristic over-fires. Every CLI wording change lands as another fix commit; misfires loop forever (reify-3604) or silently return junk success.
findings.proposal: Invert the precedence and make prose-matching a monitored fallback: (1) primary classification from structured fields already parsed into AgentResult — is_error, subtype, api_error_status==429, returncode — extending _parse_claude_output to surface any rate-limit metadata the CLI exposes; (2) when ONLY the prose matcher fires (no structured corroboration) or _parse_resets_at hits its 1h fallback, emit a distinct loud cost-store event ('cap_prose_only' / 'resets_parse_failed') and persist the raw unmatched text, so a wording change surfaces as one alert instead of a silent retry storm followed by a whack-a-mole commit; (3) pin a contract test that runs the real CLI's cap fixture set per CLI version bump (e3df395c9f already added credential integration tests — extend into a versioned fixture corpus). This doesn't eliminate the upstream gap (it can't) but converts an unbounded arms race into a bounded, observable fallback.

findings.title: Host-wide shared 6-account pool with per-process in-memory cap state and a shared mutable probe credentials file
findings.problem: Roughly 6 orchestrator processes plus fused-memory's curator/reconciliation runners each construct an independent UsageGate over the SAME account pool, with no shared state: check_at_startup is an explicit no-op (usage_gate.py:264-275), so each process re-discovers each cap by burning a real, mid-task agent invocation, and each runs its own resume-probe loop (N processes × M capped accounts haiku probes). Worse, every gate builds TaskConfigDir('usage-gate-probe') (usage_gate.py:227) which resolves to the FIXED path /tmp/claude-config-usage-gate-probe (config_dir.py:34-37) — all processes' probes, and the SIGHUP parallel all-account probe gather (usage_gate.py:706-709), concurrently rewrite the same .credentials.json with different tokens (usage_gate.py:918-919). Probe correctness silently depends on CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN env precedence over the racing credentials file — an assumption asserted nowhere; if the CLI ever prefers or writes back to the config-dir credential, probes test/attribute the wrong account fleet-wide.
findings.proposal: Two steps. Cheap now: make the probe config dir unique per account+process (TaskConfigDir(f'usage-gate-probe-{acct.name}-{os.getpid()}')) and add a comment-level assertion/regression test that env token wins over config-dir credentials. Systemic: add an `account_status` table to the existing shared CostStore SQLite (capped_until, auth_failed_at, updated_by), written through the F1 transition function; before_invoke consults it so a cap discovered by one process is honored by all, and a single-prober election (shared.locking file lock keyed by account) makes exactly one process run the resume probe per capped account, publishing the uncap.
findings.bug_history_link: Operator memory 'usage_gate account-pool weekly cap 2026-07-03' (fleet-wide 429 triage pain); 49b3858f6f 'per-task config dir, fresh probes, and admission control' fixed the sibling per-task credential race but left the probe dir shared. The concurrent-probe credential race itself is speculative (no confirmed incident), the N× rediscovery cost is confirmed by design.

clusters.architecture_notes: MemoryService is a single god-class (2947 lines, ~45 methods) that owns the durable write queue, dual-store routing (Graphiti+Mem0), journaling, and all post-write remediation logic; GraphitiBackend (1889 lines) wraps graphiti_core plus a hand-rolled per-group_id FalkorDB driver-clone cache and exposes ~50 thin Cypher-backed methods. server/tools.py (4013 lines) is a third layer of ~90 @mcp.tool functions that validate params, call memory_service/graphiti, log, and uniformly translate exceptions to error dicts. Writes flow through DurableWriteQueue (SQLite WAL, per-group_id worker pool, code default 3 workers though config.yaml currently pins 1) into _execute_graphiti_write, which chains four independent post-hoc 'healing sweep' passes after every add_episode (dedupe edges, restore superseded dependency edges, dedupe entity nodes, canonicalize task-node names) because graphiti_core's ingestion-time entity resolution has no exact-name/uniqueness check at write time. Reads (get_entity, search) fan out via asyncio.gather(return_exceptions=True) with a hand-copied two-pass CancelledError-then-first-exception pattern repeated at several call sites across memory_service.py, graphiti_client.py and reconciliation/context_assembler.py, sharing only the low-level propagate_cancellations primitive, not the full idiom. The merge/rebuild-summary pipeline is comparatively mature: _build_stale_entry/_canonical_facts are properly deduplicated shared helpers, and update_edge's TOCTOU behaviour is explicitly documented and accepted rather than silently wrong.
clusters.cross_system_notes: The core duplicate-node/duplicate-edge problem is fm-memory compensating for a missing guarantee in the vendored graphiti_core library: its resolve_extracted_nodes step only does fuzzy hybrid (embedding+BM25) candidate search, never an exact-name Cypher lookup, and its merge/redirect path (implemented locally, not upstream) deliberately copies old.uuid onto new edge elements, breaking the 'uuid is unique per edge' invariant graph-wide. fm-memory never patches graphiti_core itself; it builds an ever-growing pile of local sweep/dedup functions around it instead (task chain 429-828, plus 2084/2110 continuing the same pattern into July). This mirrors fm-recon's own reported edge-dedup-query-gap theme -- the same missing-uniqueness root cause surfaces in both places because both read through GraphitiBackend's edge-fetch methods.

findings.title: No write-time identity guarantee for entity nodes -> 4-function reactive sweep chain
findings.problem: _execute_graphiti_write (memory_service.py:832-858) chains four independent best-effort post-hoc passes after every add_episode: _dedup_episode_edges (line 484), _restore_superseded_dependency_edges (612), _dedup_episode_nodes (531), _normalize_task_node_names (687). Each is a near-identical copy of the same shape (extract touched names/edges from the just-returned result, look them up again via find_duplicate_entity_nodes, best-effort merge with except Exception: log and continue). The _dedup_episode_nodes docstring states the root cause: graphiti_core's ingestion-time entity resolution only resolves each extracted node against hybrid embedding+BM25 candidates -- there is no guaranteed exact-name Cypher lookup. No FalkorDB uniqueness constraint on Entity.name exists (build_indices_and_constraints at graphiti_client.py:195 is stubbed to a no-op for the multi-tenant driver). Because each sweep only re-scans names/uuids touched by the episode that just completed, a duplicate created across two unrelated episodes, or by a concurrent sibling worker if workers_per_group is ever raised above 1, is invisible to all four sweeps and survives until a human manually merges it in FalkorDB.
findings.proposal: Enforce node identity at creation time, not after the fact: add a single _resolve_or_create_entity(name, group_id) chokepoint in GraphitiBackend that does an exact-name Cypher lookup (get_nodes_by_exact_name, already implemented at graphiti_client.py:1175) BEFORE minting a new node, guarded by a FalkorDB uniqueness constraint on (group_id, Entity.name) or a per-group_id asyncio.Lock serializing the check-then-create window. Retire or fold the four reactive sweeps into one _reconcile_episode_identity(result, group_id) helper once the write-time gate exists, since they would then only catch pre-existing legacy duplicates rather than being the sole defense.

findings.title: merge_entities' redirect_node_edges deliberately breaks edge-uuid uniqueness, forcing every edge-read query to hand-roll graph-element dedup
findings.problem: redirect_node_edges (lines 897-903, 934-940) copies new.uuid = old.uuid when redirecting an edge onto the surviving node during a merge -- it deliberately mints a second graph relationship element carrying an already-used uuid. Edge.uuid can therefore no longer be treated as unique across the graph, so every edge-reading query must defend against it: get_valid_edges_for_node (720-730) and get_all_valid_edges (799-811) both carry multi-paragraph comments explaining why they must 'WITH DISTINCT e' / 'WITH DISTINCT n, e' (graph-element identity) instead of deduping by the (uuid, fact, name) property tuple, explicitly because redirect_node_edges copies uuids. Two prior commits (cfed95c706 removing a misplaced/wrong DISTINCT, and task-2084 pair be71e7850a/c3193549a7 adding correct DISTINCT) show this has already been gotten wrong twice in production.
findings.proposal: Stop copying old.uuid in redirect_node_edges; mint a fresh uuid for the redirected edge and carry superseded_edge_uuid=old.uuid as an audit property instead. That restores 'uuid is unique per edge' as a graph-wide invariant, lets every current and future edge query use a plain uuid-keyed dedup instead of the fragile hand-written WITH DISTINCT idiom, and removes the class of bug that produced cfed95c706 / be71e7850a / c3193549a7.
